definition_zh: 生物量；生物质；生物质燃料
definition_en: the total mass of living matter in a given area, or living material used as fuel
core_image: 一整个生态系统被放上秤，读数就是活物的总重量
scene: 这里指「生物量」。 The researchers weighed every plant in the plot to estimate the biomass of the meadow.
sceneCN: 这里 biomass 是「生物量」（第 1 个义项：一个地区的活物质总质量）；句意：研究人员称量了样方里的每一株植物，以估算这片草甸的生物量。场景要点：样方框、电子秤、割下的草、记录板、烘干箱。

pos.zh: 生物量；（可作燃料的）生物质

senses.title: Total mass of living matter
senses.titleCN: 生物量：一个地区的活物质总量
senses.definition: the total mass of living organisms in a given area or volume
senses.definitionCN: 某一区域或体积内全部活物质的总质量
senses.example: The researchers weighed every plant in the plot to estimate biomass.
senses.exampleCN: 研究人员称量了样方里的每一株植物来估算生物量。
senses.why: bio- is 'life' and mass is 'a lump, a quantity of matter'. The compound simply asks how much living stuff there is, measured as mass rather than counted as individuals. The core image is a scale under an entire ecosystem.
senses.whyCN: bio- 是“生命”，mass 是“一团、一定量的物质”。这个复合词只问“活的东西有多少”，用质量来衡量，而不是数个体。核心意象是在整个生态系统下面放一台秤。

senses.title: Biomass of a species or population
senses.titleCN: 种群生物量：某一个物种的总重量
senses.definition: the total mass of one species or population in a given area
senses.definitionCN: 某一物种或种群在特定区域内的总质量
senses.example: The fish population's biomass fell by half in a decade.
senses.exampleCN: 这个鱼类种群的生物量十年间减少了一半。
senses.why: The total can be restricted to one group. The same measure is applied to a species, so biomass becomes a stock estimate rather than a whole-ecosystem figure, and fisheries use it to decide catch limits.
senses.whyCN: 总量可以被限定在一个群体上。同一把尺子用在一个物种上，biomass 就从“整个生态系统的数字”变成“资源存量估计”，渔业用它来定捕捞上限。

senses.title: Biomass at a trophic level
senses.titleCN: 营养级生物量：食物链每一层的重量
senses.definition: the mass of living matter grouped by trophic level in a food chain
senses.definitionCN: 按食物链营养级分组的活物质质量
senses.example: A pyramid of biomass shows less living matter at each higher level.
senses.exampleCN: 生物量金字塔显示，每高一层，活物质就越少。
senses.why: Ecologists arrange species by what they eat. Grouping biomass by trophic level turns a total into a structure, and the pyramid is the standard picture of that structure: producers below, predators above.
senses.whyCN: 生态学家按“吃什么”把物种排成层。把生物量按营养级分组，就把一个总数变成一种结构，而金字塔是这种结构的标准图像：生产者在下，捕食者在上。

senses.title: Plant or crop biomass
senses.titleCN: 植物与作物生物量：可收获的植物物质
senses.definition: the mass of plants or crops grown in a field, often measured to predict yield
senses.definitionCN: 田地里生长的植物或作物的质量，常用来预测产量
senses.example: Farmers measure above-ground biomass to predict the harvest.
senses.exampleCN: 农民测量地上生物量来预测收成。
senses.why: Plants are the entry point of energy into an ecosystem, and their mass is what agriculture harvests. The compound therefore becomes a yield measure in agronomy, often qualified as above-ground or below-ground.
senses.whyCN: 植物是能量进入生态系统的入口，而农业收获的正是它们的质量。于是这个复合词在农学里成为产量指标，常以“地上／地下”来限定。

senses.title: Soil microbial biomass
senses.definition: the mass of microorganisms living in soil, used as an indicator of soil health
senses.definitionCN: 土壤中微生物的质量，用作土壤健康的指标
senses.example: Soil microbial biomass is a sensitive indicator of soil health.
senses.exampleCN: 土壤微生物生物量是土壤健康的一项敏感指标。
senses.why: Most living mass is invisible and below ground. Extending the word to microbes makes it a soil-health indicator, because microbes respond quickly to disturbance, fertilization and contamination.
senses.whyCN: 大部分活物质是看不见的，而且在地下。把词扩展到微生物，它就变成土壤健康指标，因为微生物对扰动、施肥和污染反应很快。

senses.title: Forest biomass and carbon stock
senses.definition: the mass of forest vegetation, especially as a measure of stored carbon
senses.definitionCN: 森林植被的质量，尤用作储存碳的度量
senses.example: The map estimates forest biomass to calculate stored carbon.
senses.exampleCN: 这张地图估算森林生物量，以计算储存的碳。
senses.why: About half of dry biomass is carbon, so weighing a forest also measures a carbon store. Climate policy made this technical equivalence central, and biomass became a number in carbon accounting.
senses.whyCN: 干生物量中约有一半是碳，所以给森林称重同时也在测量碳库。气候政策使这一技术等价关系变得关键，biomass 于是成为碳核算里的一个数字。

senses.title: Biomass as fuel feedstock
senses.titleCN: 生物质原料：可作燃料的生物材料
senses.definition: living or recently living material used as a source of fuel
senses.definitionCN: 用作燃料来源的活体或刚死去的生物材料
senses.example: The plant burns crop residues and wood chips as biomass.
senses.exampleCN: 这家工厂把作物残余和木屑作为生物质燃烧。
senses.why: The word shifts from a measure to a material: what was counted as living mass becomes a stock of fuel. The physical substance, not the ecological total, is now the referent, and the word behaves like 'coal'.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从“度量”转成“材料”：原本被计为活物质总量的东西，变成一堆燃料库存。此时指称的是实物，而不是生态总量，这个词在句中就像 coal 一样使用。

senses.title: Biomass power generation
senses.titleCN: 生物质发电：以生物质为燃料的技术
senses.definition: the use of biomass as fuel in boilers or power plants to produce heat and electricity
senses.definitionCN: 在锅炉或电厂中以生物质为燃料生产热与电
senses.example: A biomass plant supplies heat to the nearby town.
senses.exampleCN: 一座生物质电厂为附近的城镇供热。
senses.why: Once biomass is a fuel, it can be burned in a plant. The compound names the technology, and the word now belongs to engineering vocabulary as much as to ecology.
senses.whyCN: 一旦生物质成为燃料，就可以在电厂里燃烧。这个复合词命名的是一项技术，此时它既属于生态学词汇，也同样属于工程词汇。

senses.title: Biomass as a policy category
senses.titleCN: 政策口径中的生物质能
senses.definition: biomass counted as a renewable energy source in statistics and regulation
senses.definitionCN: 在统计与法规中被计为可再生能源的生物质
senses.example: Biomass counts as renewable in the national energy statistics.
senses.exampleCN: 在国家能源统计中，生物质被算作可再生能源。
senses.why: Policy needs categories. Biomass becomes an accounting box defined by origin rather than by ecology, and the word now answers a regulatory question: does this fuel count as renewable?
senses.whyCN: 政策需要分类。生物质于是变成一个按“来源”而非按“生态”定义的统计格子；这个词此时回答的是一个监管问题：这种燃料算不算可再生能源？

intro.en: Biomass is a 20th-century compound: Greek bio- 'life' joined to the Latin-derived English mass. It is not an inherited word, and the exact first coinage is uncertain; only the date by which it was in use is fairly well recorded.
intro.cn: biomass 是 20 世纪复合词：希腊语 bio-“生命”接上源自拉丁语的英语 mass。它不是承袭词，确切的首创情况存疑；只有“已在使用”的年代记录比较可靠。

items.en: bios means 'life, lifetime, way of life' (PIE *gwei- 'to live'). In scientific compounds bio- has meant 'organic life' since about 1800, and it is the first element of biomass.
items.cn: bios 意为“生命、寿命、生活方式”（原始印欧语 *gwei-“活”）。在科学复合词中，bio- 自约 1800 年起表示“有机生命”，是 biomass 的第一成分。

items.en: Latin massa means 'kneaded dough, lump, that which adheres together like dough', probably from Greek maza 'barley cake', related to massein 'to knead' (PIE *mag- 'to knead, fashion, fit').
items.cn: 拉丁 massa 意为“揉好的面团、团块、像面团那样黏在一起的东西”，可能来自希腊语 maza“大麦饼”，与 massein“揉”相关（原始印欧语 *mag-“揉、塑造、使合适”）。

items.en: English mass (late 14c) came from Old French masse and directly from Latin. It extended to 'a large quantity' in the 1580s, to 'bulk' about 1600, and to the physics sense 'quantity of matter' in 1704 — the sense biomass needs.
items.cn: 英语 mass（14 世纪晚期）来自古法语 masse，并直接借自拉丁语。16 世纪 80 年代扩展为“大量”，约 1600 年扩展为“体积、主体”，1704 年获得物理学义“物质的量”——正是 biomass 所需的那一层。

items.en: Etymonline records bio-mass 'by 1969' for 'the total weight of the organic substance or organisms in a given area'. Earlier uses may exist in mid-20th-century ecology and fisheries; the exact first coinage and first printed use are uncertain.
items.cn: Etymonline 把 bio-mass 记作“by 1969”，义为“某一区域内有机物质或生物的总重量”。20 世纪中期的生态学与渔业文献中可能有更早用法；确切首创与最早印刷记录存疑。

items.en: The modern energy sense moves from a measure to a commodity: what was counted as living mass becomes a stock of fuel. The link is practical — fuel is bought and sold by weight, so the measured mass turns into the traded substance.
items.cn: 现代能源义从“度量”转向“商品”：原本被计为活物质总量的东西，变成一堆燃料库存。联系是实用性的——燃料按重量买卖，于是被测量的质量变成了被交易的物质。

items.en: After the oil shocks of the 1970s, biomass entered energy policy as a renewable category alongside solar and wind. It is now standard in carbon accounting, bioenergy statistics and assessments of forest carbon stocks.
items.cn: 1970 年代石油危机之后，biomass 作为可再生能源类别与太阳能、风能并列进入能源政策。如今它已是碳核算、生物能源统计和森林碳储量评估中的标准词。

note.en: The first group contains bio- compounds and the base noun mass, which are easy to swap; the second contains ecological quantities that are often confused with biomass in measurement.
note.cn: 第一组是容易互换的 bio- 复合词与基础名词 mass；第二组是测量中常与 biomass 混淆的生态量。

entries.definition: A lump, a large quantity, or (in physics) the quantity of matter. Biomass adds bio- to restrict the mass to living material.
entries.definitionCN: 团块、大量，或物理学上的“物质的量”。biomass 加 bio- 把质量限定为活物质。

entries.definition: Gas produced by the breakdown of organic matter, mainly methane. It is a fuel made from biomass, not biomass itself.
entries.definitionCN: 有机物分解产生的气体，主要是甲烷。它是由生物质制成的燃料，而不是生物质本身。

entries.definition: Fuel made from living or recently living material. Biomass is the raw material; biofuel is the refined product.
entries.definitionCN: 由活体或刚死去的生物材料制成的燃料。biomass 是原料，biofuel 是加工后的产品。

entries.definition: The zone of life on Earth. It names a region, whereas biomass names a quantity within that region.
entries.definitionCN: 地球上的生命圈层。它命名一个区域，而 biomass 命名该区域内的一个量。

entries.definition: The amount of living matter present at a given moment. It is the actual measurement that a biomass estimate tries to represent.
entries.definitionCN: 某一时刻实际存在的活物量。它是 biomass 估计所试图表达的实际测量值。

entries.definition: The living organisms of a region as a group. It names the set of organisms, not their weight.
entries.definitionCN: 一个区域内作为整体的全部生物。它命名生物集合，而不是它们的重量。

entries.definition: Carbon-based material in soil or water, including dead and dissolved matter. Broader than biomass, which usually means living or recently living material.
entries.definitionCN: 土壤或水中含碳的物质，包括死亡与溶解的部分。比 biomass 宽，后者通常指活的或刚死去的材料。

entries.definition: The amount harvested or produced, usually for human use. It measures what is taken, while biomass measures what is there.
entries.definitionCN: 收获或产出的量，通常供人使用。它衡量被取走的部分，而 biomass 衡量现存的部分。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, the real mass family, and real measurement contrasts.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实的 mass 词族，以及真实的测量对比。

normal.en: bio- 'life' + mass 'lump of matter': life put on a scale and weighed.
normal.cn: bio-“生命”+ mass“一团物质”：把生命放上秤称重。

normal.en: mass has been in English since the late 14th century; the physics sense 'quantity of matter' dates from 1704 and is the one biomass uses.
normal.cn: mass 自 14 世纪晚期就在英语里；物理学义“物质的量”始于 1704 年，正是 biomass 所用的那一层。

normal.en: Contrast pair: biomass measures amount, biodiversity measures variety. Same prefix, different question.
normal.cn: 对比记忆：biomass 量数量，biodiversity 量多样。同一个前缀，不同的问题。

normal.en: Field convention: above-ground biomass and below-ground biomass are counted separately, so the word always needs a boundary.
normal.cn: 野外惯例：地上生物量与地下生物量分开计，所以这个词总需要一条边界。

normal.en: Energy chain: biomass (raw material) → biofuel or biogas (product) → bioenergy (the category).
normal.cn: 能源链：biomass（原料）→ biofuel 或 biogas（产品）→ bioenergy（类别）。

abstract.en: Picture an entire forest lifted onto an industrial scale; the number on the dial is biomass.
abstract.cn: 想象整片森林被抬上一台工业秤；表盘上的数字就是 biomass。

abstract.en: Picture a pyramid of trays, each holding less grain as you go up: that is the biomass pyramid.
abstract.cn: 想象一摞托盘堆成金字塔，越往上每一层的谷物越少：那就是生物量金字塔。

abstract.en: Picture a sack of wood chips beside a coal sack: both are fuel sold by weight, which is why 'mass' became 'biomass'.
abstract.cn: 想象一袋木屑放在一袋煤旁边：两者都是按重量卖的燃料，这正是“质量”变成“生物质”的原因。

examples.en: Tropical forests hold a large share of the world's living biomass.
examples.cn: 热带森林拥有全球活生物量的很大一部分。

examples.en: The village burns agricultural biomass instead of coal in winter.
examples.cn: 这个村子冬天烧农业生物质而不是煤。

examples.en: Satellites can estimate forest biomass from the height and density of the canopy.
examples.cn: 卫星可以根据树冠的高度和密度估算森林生物量。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拜（bio）生命，欧（o）麦（m）斯（ss）——把生命放到秤上称重 → biomass 生物量、生物质

root: 希腊 bios“生命”+ 拉丁 massa“面团、团块”演变来的 mass“质量”；20 世纪新造复合词，先指生态总量，后指可作燃料的生物质。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses share one measure: how much living matter there is. It is applied to a whole area, one species, one trophic level, one part of a plant, soil, or a forest; then the measured matter becomes a fuel, a technology, and a policy category.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项共享同一把尺子：活物质有多少。它被用于整片区域、一个物种、一个营养级、植物的一部分、土壤或森林；随后被测量之物又变成燃料、技术和政策类别。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: living matter put on a scale.
core.cn: 核心意象：把活物质放上秤。

branches.en: WHAT IS WEIGHED: the whole community, or one species singled out as a stock.
branches.cn: 称的是什么：整个群落，或被单独拿出作为存量的一个物种。

branches.en: STRUCTURE: grouping by trophic level turns the total into a pyramid.
branches.cn: 结构：按营养级分组，把总量变成一个金字塔。

branches.en: POOLS: crops, soil microbes and forests are separate measured pools, and each has its own method.
branches.cn: 库：作物、土壤微生物与森林是各自独立的测量库，各有自己的方法。

branches.en: CONVERSION: measured matter becomes feedstock, then heat and electricity.
branches.cn: 转化：被测量的物质变成原料，再变成热与电。

branches.en: ACCOUNTING: policy turns biomass into a renewable category with rules.
branches.cn: 核算：政策把生物质变成一个带规则的可再生类别。

intro.en: Biomass is a two-part modern compound: bio- + mass. Both halves are productive in English, so the word can be understood without knowing Latin or Greek; its compound status, not its age, is what makes it transparent.
intro.cn: biomass 是两段式现代复合词：bio- + mass。两半在英语里都能产，所以不懂拉丁语或希腊语也能理解；使它透明的，是复合词的身份，而不是年代。

latinIntro.en: Only the second element is Latin: massa 'kneaded dough, lump', probably from Greek maza. The first element is Greek bios. The compound was assembled in English, which is why no single Latin word corresponds to biomass.
latinIntro.cn: 只有第二成分是拉丁语：massa“面团、团块”，可能来自希腊语 maza。第一成分是希腊语 bios。这个复合词是在英语里拼合的，所以没有单个拉丁词与 biomass 对应。

items.structure: Latin massa (lump, dough) → Old French masse
items.meaning: a lump; a large quantity; (physics) quantity of matter
items.example: The stone has a mass of about two kilograms.
items.exampleCN: 这块石头的质量约为两公斤。

items.meaning: total living matter; living material used as fuel
items.meaningCN: 生物量；（可作燃料的）生物质
items.example: The meadow's biomass doubles each spring.
items.exampleCN: 这片草甸的生物量每年春天翻倍。

items.example: Bioenergy supplies a small but growing share of electricity.
items.exampleCN: 生物能源在电力中占一小部分，但正在增长。

items.meaning: fuel made from living or recently living material
items.example: The buses run on a biofuel blend.
items.exampleCN: 这些公交车使用混合生物燃料。

items.meaning: gas, mainly methane, produced by decomposing organic matter
items.example: The farm produces biogas from manure.
items.exampleCN: 这个农场用粪便生产沼气。

items.meaning: the zone of life on Earth
items.example: Forests are a major part of the biosphere.
items.exampleCN: 森林是生物圈的重要组成部分。

items.example: Biomass and biodiversity are measured differently.
items.exampleCN: 生物量与生物多样性的测量方式不同。

items.example: A massive oak stood at the edge of the field.
items.exampleCN: 田野边矗立着一棵巨大的橡树。

items.example: Mass production lowered the price of the device.
items.exampleCN: 大批量生产降低了这种设备的价格。

definition_zh: 美容师；护肤专家；美学家（亦作 esthetician）
definition_en: a person trained in skin care and beauty treatment; also a specialist in the philosophy of beauty, more often spelled esthetician in American use
core_image: 专门打理「看起来如何」的那个人
scene: 护理室的灯调得很柔，她先看了看客人的皮肤再开口。 The aesthetician recommended a gentler routine.
sceneCN: 这里 aesthetician 是「美容师」（第 1 个义项：受过皮肤护理与美容训练的专业人员）；句意为美容师建议了一套更温和的护理流程。核心画面是专门打理「看起来如何」的那个人。

pos.zh: 美容师；护肤专家；美学家

derivatives.zh: 去掉 -ian 的形容词，义为「审美的；美学的」
加 -s 构成，义为「美学；审美观」
加 -ally 构成，义为「在审美上」

senses.title: A specialist in skin care and beauty treatment
senses.definition: a person professionally trained to treat and care for the skin, especially the face
senses.definitionCN: 受过专业训练、从事皮肤（尤指面部）护理与治疗的人
senses.example: The aesthetician explained which acids suited sensitive skin.
senses.exampleCN: 美容师解释了哪些酸类适合敏感肌。
senses.why: Aisthetikos means able to perceive, so an aesthetician is literally a person who works on what is perceived, which in a salon means the surface others see.
senses.whyCN: aisthetikos 意为「能感知的」，所以 aesthetician 字面上是「打理被感知之物的人」，在美容院里就是别人看得见的那层表面。

senses.title: A specialist in the philosophy of beauty
senses.definition: a scholar who studies beauty and taste, a sense closer to the original philosophical use of aesthetic
senses.definitionCN: 研究美与趣味的学者，此义更接近 aesthetic 最初的哲学用法
senses.example: The aesthetician argued that ugliness has its own grammar.
senses.exampleCN: 那位美学家主张丑也有自己的语法。
senses.why: This sense keeps the word on its older path: the same perceiving root applied to judging art rather than to treating skin.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项让词留在更古老的路上：同一个「感知」词根用于评判艺术，而非护理皮肤。

intro.en: Aesthetician grew out of a Greek word for perceiving, and it split into two careers: one in a salon, one in a study.
intro.cn: aesthetician 源自一个表示「感知」的希腊语词，后来分成两种职业：一种在美容院，一种在书房。

items.en: Greek aisthanesthai meant to perceive or to feel, the verb behind the whole family.
items.cn: 希腊语 aisthanesthai 意为「感知、感觉」，是整个词族背后的动词。

items.en: Greek aisthetikos meant perceptive or sensitive, built on the verb of perceiving.
items.cn: 希腊语 aisthetikos 意为「有感知力的、敏感的」，建立在感知动词上。

items.en: Aesthetic entered English in the eighteenth century through German discussions of beauty and taste.
items.cn: aesthetic 于十八世纪经德语关于美与趣味的讨论进入英语。

items.en: The suffix -ian names a person practising or expert in something, as in musician and physician.
items.cn: 后缀 -ian 表示从事或精通某事的人，如 musician、physician。

items.en: Aesthetician is recorded from the nineteenth century; in twentieth century American use it narrowed mainly to skin care, often spelled esthetician.
items.cn: aesthetician 见于十九世纪；在二十世纪美式用法中主要收窄为皮肤护理，常拼作 esthetician。

note.en: The look-alike group stays inside the perceiving family, including the spelling without the a; the near-meaning group lists other skin and beauty professionals.
note.cn: 形近组留在「感知」词族内，包括省去 a 的拼写；近义组列出其他皮肤与美容专业人员。

entries.definition: Concerned with beauty and the appreciation of it.
entries.definitionCN: 与美及其欣赏有关的。

entries.definition: The usual American spelling of the same noun.
entries.definitionCN: 同一名词的美式常用拼写。

entries.definition: A drug that removes sensation, with an- meaning without.
entries.definitionCN: 消除感觉的药物，an- 表示「无」。

entries.definition: A person whose job is beauty treatment, a broader term.
entries.definitionCN: 以美容为业的人，含义更宽。

entries.definition: A professional trained in cosmetic treatment of skin, hair and nails.
entries.definitionCN: 受过皮肤、毛发与指甲美容训练的专业人员。

entries.definition: A doctor specializing in skin disease rather than beauty care.
entries.definitionCN: 专治皮肤疾病而非美容护理的医生。

normalIntro.en: Aesthetician is aesthetic plus -ian: the person who does aesthetics, whether on a face or in a book.
normalIntro.cn: aesthetician 就是 aesthetic 加 -ian：做美学这件事的人，无论在脸上还是在书里。

normal.en: Music plus -ian gives musician; aesthetic plus -ian gives aesthetician.
normal.cn: music 加 -ian 得 musician；aesthetic 加 -ian 得 aesthetician。

normal.en: The aes- at the front is the same as in anaesthetic, only without the negation.
normal.cn: 词首的 aes- 与 anaesthetic 中相同，只是没有否定前缀。

normal.en: In American salons you will usually see esthetician without the a.
normal.cn: 在美式美容院里你通常会看到省去 a 的 esthetician。

normal.en: An aesthetician treats skin; a dermatologist treats disease.
normal.cn: aesthetician 护理皮肤；dermatologist 治疗疾病。

normal.en: The older sense is a thinker about beauty, not a treater of faces.
normal.cn: 更古老的义项是思考美的人，而不是护理脸的人。

abstract.en: Picture a person whose whole job is the surface that others perceive.
abstract.cn: 想象一个全部工作就是别人所感知的那层表面的人。

abstract.en: Imagine a lamp turned low so that every texture can be judged fairly.
abstract.cn: 想象一盏调暗的灯，让每种质地都能被公平评判。

abstract.en: Think of the same word walking from a philosophy lecture into a treatment room.
abstract.cn: 想象同一个词从哲学讲堂走进护理室。

examples.en: The aesthetician kept a record of every product she used.
examples.cn: 美容师记录了她使用的每一种产品。

examples.en: An aesthetician must understand both chemistry and skin.
examples.cn: 美容师必须同时懂化学与皮肤。

examples.en: The eighteenth century aesthetician wrote only about taste.
examples.cn: 十八世纪的美学家只写趣味问题。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「爱斯塞提申」——爱（aes）斯（the）塞（ti）提申（cian），专门打理「看起来怎样」的那个人，就是美容师、美学家。

root: 希腊语 aisthanesthai「感知」派生 aisthetikos「有感知力的」，经德语美学讨论进入英语 aesthetic，再加表示人的后缀 -ian 构成 aesthetician，字面即「从事感知与美的人」。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses share one root idea of perceiving: one works on the surface that is perceived, the other on the judgement of what is perceived.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项共享「感知」这一词根想法：一个打理被感知的表面，另一个研究对被感知之物的判断。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person who works on what is perceived
core.cn: 核心意象：打理被感知之物的人

branches.en: Perceiving applied to skin as a surface.
branches.cn: 把感知用于作为表面的皮肤。

branches.en: Perceiving applied to judging art.
branches.cn: 把感知用于评判艺术。

branches.en: Both keep the Greek root of sensation.
branches.cn: 两者都保留希腊语「感觉」词根。

branches.en: The narrower modern American career.
branches.cn: 更窄的现代美式职业。

branches.en: The older philosophical career.
branches.cn: 更古老的哲学职业。

intro.en: Aesthetician is a Greek root of sensation plus a person suffix, and negating the same root produces the word for losing feeling.
intro.cn: aesthetician 是希腊语「感觉」词根加表人后缀，而否定同一词根就得到表示失去感觉的词。

latinIntro.en: The root is Greek aisthesis, sensation; Latin borrowed it as aesthesis, which is why the spelling keeps the aes- cluster.
latinIntro.cn: 词根是希腊语 aisthesis「感觉」；拉丁语借为 aesthesis，因此拼写保留 aes- 这一字母组合。

latinEntries.example: Aisthesis is the root of aesthetic.
latinEntries.exampleCN: aisthesis 是 aesthetic 的词根。
aisthetikos 提供了 aesthetic 的词干。

definition_zh: 经纪业务；经纪公司；佣金，回扣
definition_en: the business of a broker; a firm of brokers; the fee a broker charges
core_image: 中间人一手牵买家一手牵卖家，从成交里抽一小截
scene: 交易大厅里电话声此起彼伏，报价屏不停闪烁。 Her brokerage handled trades for two hundred clients.
sceneCN: 这里 brokerage 是「经纪公司」（第 2 个义项：经营代理买卖业务的公司）；句意是她所在的经纪公司为两百名客户打理交易。

pos.zh: 经纪业务；经纪公司；经纪人佣金

derivatives.zh: brokerage 的基础词，义为「经纪人；掮客」
由 broker 加 -ship 构成，义为「经纪身份；经纪行当（罕用）」
由动词加 -ing 构成，义为「居间撮合的行为」

senses.title: The broker's business
senses.definition: the trade of acting as an agent between buyers and sellers
senses.definitionCN: 在买卖双方之间居间代理的业务
senses.example: The firm moved from banking into brokerage.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司从银行业转入了经纪业务。
senses.why: The agent suffix -age turns the broker into his line of work.
senses.whyCN: 集体或行为后缀 -age 把经纪人转成他的业务行当。

senses.title: A firm of brokers
senses.definition: a company whose business is brokerage
senses.definitionCN: 经营经纪业务的公司机构
senses.example: She opened an account at a discount brokerage.
senses.exampleCN: 她在一家折扣券商开了账户。
senses.why: A business name easily becomes the name of the business place.
senses.whyCN: 业务的名称顺势转指经营这项业务的机构。

senses.title: The broker's fee
senses.definition: the fee or commission charged for arranging a deal
senses.definitionCN: 为撮合交易而收取的酬金
senses.example: The deal cost them a hefty brokerage.
senses.exampleCN: 这笔交易让他们付了一笔可观的佣金。
senses.why: -age also names payment for a service, like postage orstorage.
senses.whyCN: -age 也可表服务酬金，如 postage、storage 之类。

intro.en: Brokerage is broker plus -age, and broker itself comes from an Old French word for small trader.
intro.cn: brokerage 由 broker 加 -age 构成，broker 则源自古法语指小贩的词。

items.en: broceour meant a small trader, wine seller or retailer.
items.cn: 古法语 broceour 指小贩、酒贩或零售商。

items.en: brocour crossed into England with the wine trade.
items.cn: 随酒业传入英格兰，词形作 brocour。

items.en: broker meant a middleman in trade, at first with a hint of trickery.
items.cn: 十四世纪英语 broker 指居间商人，起初略带贬义。

items.en: brokerage formed on broker with the -age suffix for business and fees.
items.cn: 十六至十七世纪以 broker 加 -age 构成 brokerage，兼指业务与佣金。

items.en: brokerage now names firms, accounts and fees in finance and property.
items.cn: 如今 brokerage 用于金融与地产，指券商、账户与佣金。

note.en: Brokerage belongs to the world of agents and middlemen.
note.cn: brokerage 属于代理与居间业务的世界。

entries.definition: an agent who buys and sells for others
entries.definitionCN: 经纪人，brokerage 的基础词

entries.definition: the act of arranging deals as a broker
entries.definitionCN: 居间撮合的行为

entries.definition: the fee or act of storing
entries.definitionCN: 仓储（费）——同为 -age 表费用，词根不同

entries.definition: the business of acting for others; an agent's firm
entries.definitionCN: 代理业务；代理机构

entries.definition: a fee paid as a percentage of a sale
entries.definitionCN: 按成交额抽取的佣金

entries.definition: a trader who buys and sells on his own account
entries.definitionCN: 自营商，与经纪人相对

entries.definition: a person who acts between two parties
entries.definitionCN: 中间人；斡旋者

entries.definition: a business company
entries.definitionCN: 商行；公司

normalIntro.en: Stack the word: broker plus age equals the broker's business, firm and fee.
normalIntro.cn: 把词拆开记：broker 加 age，即经纪人的业务、公司与佣金。

normal.en: Broker + age: like postage, a fee word.
normal.cn: broker 加 -age，如 postage 一样可表费用。

normal.en: A brokerage account is where the broker works for you.
normal.cn: brokerage account 就是券商替你操作交易的账户。

normal.en: Real estate brokerage sells houses for a cut.
normal.cn: 地产中介抽成卖房。

normal.en: Dealer trades his own goods; broker trades yours.
normal.cn: dealer 卖自己的货，broker 卖你的货。

normal.en: Age here means business, not years.
normal.cn: 这里的 -age 表业务，与年龄无关。

abstract.en: See a middleman shaking two hands at once.
abstract.cn: 想象中间人同时握住两只手。

abstract.en: Watch a thin slice peel off every big deal.
abstract.cn: 看着每笔大交易上削下薄薄一片。

abstract.en: Hear ringing phones in a room full of screens.
abstract.cn: 听满屋屏幕间电话铃声大作。

examples.en: The brokerage earned a fee on every share traded.
examples.cn: 券商从每笔股票交易中抽取佣金。

examples.en: He left banking to open a small brokerage downtown.
examples.cn: 他离开银行业，在市中心开了家小经纪行。

examples.en: They cut brokerage costs by trading online.
examples.cn: 他们改做线上交易以省下经纪费。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「不若亏之」——中间人劝你：「不若亏之」，亏他一点佣金，买卖才成。

root: brokerage 由 broker（经纪人）加 -age（业务、费用）构成；broker 源自古法语 broceour／brocour（小贩、酒商），更早词源不确定，或与灌木丛（broce）中摆摊的零售者有关，属存疑假说。

sensesIntro.en: The -age suffix spreads one root across the business, the firm and the fee.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个 -age 后缀，让同一个词根覆盖了业务、公司和佣金三义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a middleman taking a thin slice of the deal.
core.cn: 核心意象：中间人从成交中抽走薄薄一片。

branches.en: go into brokerage
branches.cn: 进入经纪行业

branches.en: an insurance brokerage
branches.cn: 保险经纪行

branches.en: a brokerage account
branches.cn: 券商账户

branches.en: charge heavy brokerage
branches.cn: 收取高额佣金

branches.en: brokerage on the deal
branches.cn: 该笔交易的佣金

intro.en: The family is small: the agent, his act, his status and his business.
intro.cn: 词族不大：经纪人、其行为、其身份、其业务。

latinIntro.en: The trail is French and possibly older still, ending in uncertainty.
latinIntro.cn: 词源经法语上溯，更早来源不确定。

items.meaning: an agent for buyers and sellers

items.meaningCN: 表业务、费用或集合的后缀
经纪业务；经纪公司；佣金

items.exampleCN: 他的经纪资格失效（罕用）

items.meaning: a person who deals in influence

definition_zh: v. 使集中；把…集中到中央；实行集中管理
definition_en: to bring power, control or activity together under one centre
core_image: 四个仓库的钥匙交到同一张桌上
scene: 公司决定把四个仓库的库存集中到一个系统里。 The company decided to centralize stock from four warehouses.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：centralize 指使集中；句意是公司把四个仓库的库存集中到一个系统。

pos.zh: 使集中；集中管理

senses.title: To bring under one control
senses.definition: to move decision-making or control into a single authority
senses.definitionCN: 把决策或控制权移入单一机构
senses.example: The ministry centralized all approvals.
senses.exampleCN: 该部把所有审批权集中起来。
senses.why: The verb is centre plus the suffix meaning to make.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词是 centre 加上表示「使…」的词缀。

senses.title: To gather in one place
senses.definition: to move records, stock or equipment into one place
senses.definitionCN: 把档案、库存或设备移到一处
senses.example: They centralized the archive in the basement.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把档案集中到地下室。
senses.why: The physical sense follows from the same inward movement.
senses.whyCN: 实物含义同样源于向内收拢的动作。

intro.en: Centralize is centre plus a verb suffix, built on Latin centrum.
intro.cn: centralize 是 centre 加动词词缀，建于拉丁语 centrum 之上。

items.en: Centrum names the middle point.
items.cn: 拉丁语 centrum 指中心点。

items.en: Central enters English meaning of the middle.
items.cn: 十七世纪 central 进入英语，意为居中的。

items.en: The verb means to place in the middle.
items.cn: 十八世纪动词意为置于中央。

items.en: Centralize names the gathering of office power.
items.cn: 十九世纪指把机关权力收归一处。

items.en: Firms centralize buying and records.
items.cn: 二十世纪企业集中采购与档案。

items.en: Centralize covers any inward gathering.
items.cn: 现代泛指任何向内集中。

note.en: The look-alike group varies the ending; the near-meaning group names gathering and its reverse.
note.cn: 形近组变化词尾；近义组列出聚集及其反面。

entries.definition: The British spelling of the verb.
entries.definitionCN: 英式拼写。

entries.definition: A system of central control.
entries.definitionCN: 中央集权制。

entries.definition: To cancel the effect of something.
entries.definitionCN: 使失效。

entries.definition: To bring things into one place.
entries.definitionCN: 集中。

entries.definition: To combine into one whole.
entries.definitionCN: 合并巩固。

entries.definition: To join parts into one.
entries.definitionCN: 统一。

normalIntro.en: Four keys end up on one desk.
normalIntro.cn: 四把钥匙最后放到同一张桌上。

normal.en: Centre is the middle point.
normal.cn: centre 是中心点。

normal.en: The suffix means to make.
normal.cn: 词缀意为使变成。

normal.en: So centralize means to make central.
normal.cn: 所以 centralize 意为使居中。

normal.en: Power and records move inward.
normal.cn: 权力与档案向内移动。

normal.en: Its reverse adds de- in front.
normal.cn: 反义词在前面加 de-。

abstract.en: Threads tied to a single post.
abstract.cn: 线都系到同一根柱上。

abstract.en: One hand holding every key.
abstract.cn: 一只手握着所有钥匙。

abstract.en: A city becoming the country brain.
abstract.cn: 一座城成了国家的大脑。

examples.en: The firm will centralize purchasing next year.
examples.cn: 公司明年将集中采购。

examples.en: They centralized the files in one office.
examples.cn: 他们把档案集中到一间办公室。

examples.en: Centralizing decisions slowed the local branches.
examples.cn: 把决策集中拖慢了地方分部。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「森戳来子」——森林里把东西戳到中央，摞成一叠子。

root: 拉丁语 centrum（中心）→ central → centralize

sensesIntro.en: The verb covers both authority and physical stock moving to one centre.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个动词既指权威也指实物收拢到一个中心。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: keys and ledgers piling on a single desk
core.cn: 核心意象：钥匙与账本堆到同一张桌上

branches.en: A single office signing every approval.
branches.cn: 一间办公室签下所有审批。

branches.en: Branch managers waiting for one call.
branches.cn: 分部经理等着同一通电话。

branches.en: Boxes carried into one warehouse.
branches.cn: 箱子搬进同一个仓库。

branches.en: One database replacing four.
branches.cn: 一个数据库取代四个。

branches.en: Everything bent toward one point.
branches.cn: 一切都弯向同一点。

intro.en: Centralize is a root plus a verb ending; the list below adds words of centre and control.
intro.cn: centralize 是词根加动词词尾；下面列出中心与控制词场的词缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin centrum is a centre, and unus is one.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 centrum 意为中心，unus 意为一。

latinEntries.exampleCN: centrum 产生 centre 与 central。
unus 产生 unity 与 uniform。
focus 产生 focus 与 focal。

definition_zh: n. 哮喘（气道慢性炎症，反复喘息、气短、胸闷）；由此产生的喘息状态
definition_en: A long-term condition in which the airways narrow and swell, causing repeated wheezing, coughing and breathlessness; also the resulting state of struggling to breathe.
core_image: 气道像被捏细的吸管，气进出都带着哨音
scene: 他一跑起来就喘，随身带着吸入器。 Running brings on his asthma, so he carries an inhaler.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：asthma 指气道反复发炎变窄的慢性病，即哮喘。

pos.zh: 哮喘；喘息状态

senses.title: The long-term airway disease
senses.definition: a chronic condition in which the airways become inflamed and narrow, so breathing is repeatedly difficult
senses.definitionCN: 气道发炎变窄的慢性病，导致呼吸反复困难
senses.example: Her asthma is worse in cold weather.
senses.exampleCN: 她的哮喘在冷天更严重。
senses.why: The Greek root means to breathe hard, so the word names the effort of breathing rather than the lungs themselves.
senses.whyCN: 希腊词根意为「费力呼吸」，所以这个词命名的是呼吸的费力，而不是肺本身。

senses.title: The resulting struggle for breath
senses.definition: the state of wheezing and tightness at a given moment, as in his asthma is playing up
senses.definitionCN: 某一时刻喘息与胸闷的状态，如「他的哮喘又闹起来了」
senses.example: The dust brought his asthma back within minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 灰尘几分钟内就把他的喘息勾了回来。
senses.why: Speakers slide from the diagnosis to the present feeling, which is why the same noun covers both.
senses.whyCN: 说话者会从诊断滑到当下的感受，所以同一个名词把两者都覆盖了。

intro.en: Asthma is Greek asthma, panting, from azein, to breathe hard, related to the verb for blowing that also gives aer, air.
intro.cn: asthma 就是希腊语 asthma「喘息」，出自 azein「费力呼吸」，与表示「吹」的动词同源，后者也给出 aer「空气」。

items.en: A reconstructed root meaning to blow or breathe lies behind words for air and for hard breathing.
items.cn: 一个意为「吹、呼吸」的拟构词根，藏在表示空气与费力呼吸的词背后。

items.en: Greek azein meant to breathe hard or pant, the physical effort the disease is named for.
items.cn: 希腊语 azein 意为「费力呼吸、喘」，正是这个病命名所依据的身体感受。

items.en: Greek asthma named panting itself, and physicians used it for the condition of laboured breathing.
items.cn: 希腊语 asthma 本指「喘息」，医生用它指呼吸费力的病症。

items.en: Latin kept the Greek term unchanged, and it travelled through medical Latin across Europe.
items.cn: 拉丁语原样沿用了这个希腊词，它随医学拉丁语传遍欧洲。

items.en: English records asthma from the fourteenth century, long spelled with the th that is now silent.
items.cn: 英语从十四世纪起记录 asthma，长期保留如今不发音的 th 拼写。

items.en: Twentieth-century medicine redefined it as chronic airway inflammation, which changed treatment from relief to control.
items.cn: 二十世纪医学把它重新定义为气道慢性炎症，使治疗从「缓解」转向「控制」。

note.en: The look-alike group warns against three words that only share the opening sound; the near-meaning group separates the symptom from neighbouring lung diseases.
note.cn: 形近组提醒不要与三个只是开头音相同的词混淆；近义组把症状与邻近的肺部疾病分开。

entries.definition: Affected by or relating to asthma.
entries.definitionCN: 患哮喘的；与哮喘有关的。

entries.definition: A dangerous lack of oxygen.
entries.definitionCN: 危险的缺氧状态。

entries.definition: The wasting away of a body part.
entries.definitionCN: 身体某部位的萎缩。

entries.definition: Too few red cells in the blood.
entries.definitionCN: 血中红细胞过少。

entries.definition: To breathe with a whistling sound.
entries.definitionCN: 带着哨音呼吸。

entries.definition: Inflammation of the larger airways.
entries.definitionCN: 较大气道的炎症。

entries.definition: Damage to the air sacs of the lungs.
entries.definitionCN: 肺泡受损的疾病。

entries.definition: The feeling of not getting enough air.
entries.definitionCN: 气不够用的感觉。

normalIntro.en: Asthma comes from a Greek verb for breathing hard, so the word names the effort, not the organ.
normalIntro.cn: asthma 出自一个表示「费力呼吸」的希腊动词，所以这个词命名的是「费力」，不是器官。

normal.en: The th is silent in both accents.
normal.cn: 两种口音里 th 都不发音。

normal.en: Asthmatic is the adjective and the person.
normal.cn: asthmatic 既是形容词也指患者。

normal.en: An asthma attack is one bout, not the disease.
normal.cn: an asthma attack 是一次发作，不是这个病。

normal.en: Asthma is uncountable, so no plural.
normal.cn: asthma 不可数，没有复数。

normal.en: Bronchitis and emphysema are different conditions.
normal.cn: bronchitis 与 emphysema 是不同的病。

abstract.en: Picture a drinking straw pinched in the middle.
abstract.cn: 想象一根中间被捏细的吸管。

abstract.en: Imagine a whistle sounding on every breath out.
abstract.cn: 想象每次呼气都响起一声哨音。

abstract.en: Think of an inhaler kept in a coat pocket.
abstract.cn: 想象外套口袋里常备的吸入器。

examples.en: Cold air can trigger asthma.
examples.cn: 冷空气可能诱发哮喘。

examples.en: He has managed his asthma for years.
examples.cn: 他多年来一直把哮喘控制得住。

examples.en: The clinic runs an asthma review each spring.
examples.cn: 这家门诊每年春天做一次哮喘复查。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音记忆：读作「阿兹玛」，想着「啊——嘶——」那口带哨音的气，就是哮喘 asthma（th 不发音）。

root: 希腊语 azein「费力呼吸」生出 asthma「喘息」，与 aer「空气」同源；拉丁语原样沿用，十四世纪入英语，拼写保留不发音的 th。

sensesIntro.en: The two senses are one narrow straw seen twice: the long-term diagnosis, and the whistling struggle of a particular moment.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项是同一根被捏细的吸管被看了两遍：长期的诊断，以及某个时刻带哨音的挣扎。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an airway pinched like a straw, every breath whistling
core.cn: 核心意象：气道像被捏细的吸管，气进出都带着哨音

branches.en: A chest tighter in cold weather.
branches.cn: 冷天里更紧的胸口。

branches.en: A childhood diagnosis carried for life.
branches.cn: 从儿童期带到成年的诊断。

branches.en: Dust bringing the wheeze back.
branches.cn: 灰尘把喘息勾回来。

branches.en: An inhaler reached for mid-run.
branches.cn: 跑到一半伸手去拿吸入器。

branches.en: One narrowed straw, a diagnosis and a moment.
branches.cn: 同一根变窄的吸管，既是诊断也是一刻。

intro.en: Asthma takes the adjective ending -atic to give asthmatic; the surrounding lung vocabulary is built from bronch-, pneu- and -itis.
intro.cn: asthma 加形容词后缀 -atic 得 asthmatic；周边的肺部词汇由 bronch-、pneu- 与 -itis 搭起。

latinIntro.en: The classical layer is Latin spirare, to breathe, and spiritus, breath; Greek bronchos, windpipe, names the tube involved.
latinIntro.cn: 古典层次是拉丁语 spirare「呼吸」与 spiritus「气息」；希腊语 bronchos「气管」指发病时受累的那根管道。

latinEntries.exampleCN: spirare 产生 respire 与 inspire。

definition_zh: 离子的；离子键的；离子型的；（建筑）爱奥尼亚式的（同形异义）
definition_en: relating to ions or to bonds formed by electrically charged atoms
core_image: 一正一负两个小球彼此吸住，中间隔着一段空隙
scene: 一正一负两个小球彼此吸住，中间隔着一段空隙。 Sodium chloride dissolves because its ionic lattice breaks apart in water.
sceneCN: 这里 ionic 指由带电离子成键的（第 1 个义项：属于离子或离子键的）；句意：氯化钠能溶解，是因为它的离子晶格在水中散开。图中可辨识物件：带正号的小球、带负号的小球、之间的空隙、晶格示意图。

pos.zh: 离子的；离子键的；离子型的；爱奥尼亚式的

senses.title: Of ions or ionic bonds
senses.definition: relating to ions, or to bonds formed by the attraction of oppositely charged ions
senses.definitionCN: 与离子有关，或与带相反电荷的离子相互吸引所形成的键有关
senses.example: Sodium chloride dissolves because its ionic lattice breaks apart in water.
senses.exampleCN: 氯化钠能溶解，是因为它的离子晶格在水中散开。
senses.why: the adjective simply attaches the noun ion to whatever it describes, with no figurative shift.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词只是把名词「离子」接到所修饰之物上，没有比喻转移。

senses.title: Of an ionic compound
senses.definition: describing a compound built from cations and anions rather than from molecules
senses.definitionCN: 指由阳离子与阴离子、而非分子构成的化合物
senses.example: The ionic compound conducts electricity only when molten.
senses.exampleCN: 这种离子化合物只在熔融时才导电。
senses.why: the adjective moved from the bond to the whole substance those bonds assemble.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词从键转移到由那些键拼成的整个物质。

senses.title: Of an ionic liquid or surfactant
senses.titleCN: 离子液体或离子型表面活性剂的
senses.definition: describing materials that are themselves made of ions but behave as liquids or as charged detergents
senses.definitionCN: 指本身由离子构成、却呈液体行为或带电荷去污作用的材料
senses.example: An ionic liquid can dissolve cellulose without boiling.
senses.exampleCN: 一种离子液体能在不沸腾的情况下溶解纤维素。
senses.why: industrial chemistry named a new class of materials after their charged makeup, keeping the same adjective.
senses.whyCN: 工业化学按带电构成给一类新材料命名，仍用同一个形容词。

senses.title: Ionic conduction
senses.definition: describing movement of charge carried by ions rather than by electrons
senses.definitionCN: 指由离子而非电子携带电荷的移动
senses.example: Ionic conduction in the membrane carries the signal along the nerve.
senses.exampleCN: 膜中的离子导电把信号沿神经传下去。
senses.why: once the charge carriers are ions, the adjective marks that mode of conduction against the electronic one.
senses.whyCN: 当载流子是离子时，这个形容词标记出这种导电方式，以区别于电子导电。

senses.title: Ionic radius
senses.definition: describing the share of a distance assigned to one ion in a crystal
senses.definitionCN: 指晶体中分配给单个离子的那部分距离
senses.example: The ionic radius of the cation decides how the crystal packs.
senses.exampleCN: 阳离子的离子半径决定晶体如何堆积。
senses.why: like the covalent radius, this is a measurement convention that uses the adjective to label the species.
senses.whyCN: 与共价半径一样，这是一种测量约定，用这个形容词标记物种。

senses.title: Ionic current in physiology
senses.definition: describing the flow of ions across a membrane or through a channel
senses.definitionCN: 指离子跨膜或穿过通道的流动
senses.example: The ionic current through the channel lasts a few milliseconds.
senses.exampleCN: 通过通道的离子流持续几毫秒。
senses.why: physiology borrowed the adjective for the charged flow that excites nerve and muscle cells.
senses.whyCN: 生理学借这个形容词指使神经与肌肉细胞兴奋的带电流动。

senses.title: The Ionic order in architecture
senses.titleCN: 建筑中的爱奥尼亚柱式
senses.definition: belonging to the classical order named after Ionia, with scroll-shaped capitals
senses.definitionCN: 属于以爱奥尼亚命名的古典柱式，柱头带涡卷
senses.example: The porch was built in the ionic style, with volutes on every capital.
senses.exampleCN: 这座门廊按爱奥尼亚式建造，每个柱头都有涡卷。
senses.why: this is a different word that happens to share the spelling: it comes from Ionia, not from ion.
senses.whyCN: 这是一个恰好拼写相同的另一个词：它出自地名「爱奥尼亚」，而非「离子」。

senses.title: Of Ionia or its dialect
senses.definition: relating to the Greek region of Ionia, its people or its dialect
senses.definitionCN: 与希腊爱奥尼亚地区、其居民或方言有关的
senses.example: The scholar compared ionic Greek with the Attic dialect.
senses.exampleCN: 这位学者把爱奥尼亚希腊语与阿提卡方言作比较。
senses.why: the oldest sense of this spelling is geographical, and it survives in histories of Greece and of architecture.
senses.whyCN: 这一拼写最古老的义项是地理的，它存留在希腊史与建筑史中。

intro.en: Ionic has two separate origins behind one spelling: an adjective of ion, the charged particle named by Faraday, and an adjective of Ionia, the Greek region. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 同一个拼写背后有两条独立来源：一是 ion（法拉第命名的带电粒子）的形容词，二是地名「爱奥尼亚」的形容词。年代均为约数。

items.en: Ienai meant to go or come; its neuter present participle ion meant a going thing. The deeper Indo-European connections are reconstructions.
items.cn: ienai 意为「去、来」，其中性现在分词 ion 意为「正在走的东西」。更早的印欧语联系属于重构。

items.en: Michael Faraday coined ion for the charged particles that travel to the electrodes during electrolysis, taking the Greek participle literally.
items.cn: 法拉第在 1834 年为电解时游向电极的带电粒子造出 ion 一词，字面取用那个希腊分词。

items.en: Greek -ikos, Latin -icus and English -ic form adjectives of relation, so ionic simply means of ions.
items.cn: 希腊 -ikos、拉丁 -icus 与英语 -ic 构成关系形容词，因此 ionic 就是「离子的」。

items.en: Ionia was the Greek region on the coast of Asia Minor; Ionic named its people, its dialect and later one of the classical architectural orders.
items.cn: 爱奥尼亚是小亚细亚沿岸的希腊地区；Ionic 指其居民、方言，后来也指一种古典建筑柱式。

items.en: The two adjectives are unrelated in origin but identical in English spelling, which is why chemistry and architecture use the same letters for different things.
items.cn: 这两个形容词来源无关，英语拼写却完全相同，所以化学与建筑用同样的字母表示不同的东西。

items.en: First date uncertain: the chemical adjective follows Faraday's coinage of 1834, but its earliest printed use is not precisely dated, so the date is approximate.
items.cn: 首见年代不确定：化学义形容词紧随法拉第 1834 年的造词，但其最早的印刷用例没有确切年代，故年代只是约数。

note.en: The first group is the ion family; the second group is the bond types and charged species that ionic is contrasted with. Note that one look-alike belongs to a different word entirely.
note.cn: 第一组是 ion 词族；第二组是与 ionic 对照的键型与带电物种。注意其中一个形近词完全属于另一个词。

entries.definition: The charged particle itself; the adjective describes anything made of or involving such particles.
entries.definitionCN: 指带电粒子本身；形容词描述由这类粒子构成或涉及它们的事物。

entries.definition: To make an atom or molecule into an ion; it names the act, while ionic names the state or type.
entries.definitionCN: 使原子或分子成为离子；它命名动作，ionic 命名状态或类型。

entries.definition: The process of producing ions; it is a noun, and cannot modify bond or compound.
entries.definitionCN: 产生离子的过程；它是名词，不能修饰 bond 或 compound。

entries.definition: Describing bonds made by shared electrons; ionic bonds are made by transfer and attraction instead.
entries.definitionCN: 描述由共享电子形成的键；离子键则由电子转移与吸引形成。

entries.definition: Describing the negatively charged ions, a subset of ionic species rather than a synonym for all of them.
entries.definitionCN: 描述带负电的离子，是离子物种的一个子集，而不是全部离子的同义词。

entries.definition: Describing the positively charged ions, the other subset, often used of surfactants and polymers.
entries.definitionCN: 描述带正电的离子，是另一个子集，常用于表面活性剂与聚合物。

entries.definition: Describing conduction or decomposition by electric current through an electrolyte; it names the method, not the bond.
entries.definitionCN: 描述电流通过电解质引起的导电或分解；命名方法，而非键型。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Greek participle, Faraday's coinage and the separate Ionia line.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的希腊分词、法拉第的造词，以及独立的地名线。

normal.en: Ion is Greek for a going thing, and the adjective simply says of ions.
normal.cn: ion 在希腊语中是「正在走的东西」，形容词就是「离子的」。

normal.en: The family runs ion, ionic, ionize, ionization, anion and cation.
normal.cn: 同族词有 ion、ionic、ionize、ionization、anion 与 cation。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the applications: ionic bond, ionic liquid, ionic conduction.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出应用：离子键、离子液体、离子导电。

normal.en: Faraday coined ion in 1834, so the chemistry sense has a date, while the Ionia sense is ancient.
normal.cn: 法拉第在 1834 年造出 ion，因此化学义有确切年代，而爱奥尼亚义则古老。

normal.en: Ionic and covalent are the two taught extremes: transfer against sharing.
normal.cn: ionic 与 covalent 是教学中两个极端：转移对共享。

abstract.en: Picture two magnets that click together across a gap.
abstract.cn: 想象两块磁铁隔着空隙咔一声吸在一起。

abstract.en: Picture a stone column whose top curls like a rolled paper.
abstract.cn: 想象一根石柱，柱顶像卷起的纸那样卷曲。

abstract.en: Picture two crowds leaving one square through opposite gates.
abstract.cn: 想象两群人从同一个广场经相反的两道门离开。

examples.en: The ionic bond breaks when water molecules pull the ions apart.
examples.cn: 当水分子把离子拉开时，离子键就断了。

examples.en: Ionic liquids stay liquid at room temperature.
examples.cn: 离子液体在室温下仍保持液态。

examples.en: The building mixes an ionic colonnade with a plain wall.
examples.cn: 这座建筑把爱奥尼亚柱廊与素墙混在一起。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「ion（离子）+ ic」——离子那一类的 → 离子的、离子键的；另有一个同形词指爱奥尼亚柱式

root: 希腊 ienai「去」→ 现在分词 ion「正在走的东西」→ 法拉第 1834 年造 ion「离子」→ 加 -ic → ionic「离子的」；另有同形词出自地名 Ionia「爱奥尼亚」，与离子无关。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one charged particle, then one look-alike word: ions and their bonds, compounds, liquids, conduction, radius, currents, and finally the Ionic order and the region of Ionia, which share spelling but not origin.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项先沿一个带电粒子展开，随后转向一个形近词：离子及其键、化合物、液体、导电、半径、离子流，最后是爱奥尼亚柱式与爱奥尼亚地区，它们同拼写而不同源。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a positive and a negative bead held apart yet pulling at each other across a gap.
core.cn: 核心意象：一正一负两颗珠子隔开，却越过空隙相互拉扯。

branches.en: THE CHARGED LINK: attraction between ions, which is the plainest chemical sense.
branches.cn: 带电的连接：离子之间的吸引，是最直白的化学义。

branches.en: WHAT THE LINK BUILDS: salts that conduct when molten, and liquids that are themselves ions.
branches.cn: 连接所造之物：熔融时导电的盐，以及本身即由离子构成的液体。

branches.en: MEASURED BEHAVIOUR: charge that moves through a membrane, and a radius taken in a crystal.
branches.cn: 被测的行为：穿过膜的电荷，以及在晶体中读取的半径。

branches.en: THE LIVING CURRENT: the flow that excites nerve and muscle.
branches.cn: 活体中的电流：使神经与肌肉兴奋的流动。

branches.en: THE OTHER WORD: a column style and a Greek region, related to neither ion nor charge.
branches.cn: 另一个词：一种柱式与一个希腊地区，与离子和电荷都无关。

intro.en: Ionic is a noun plus a Greek adjective ending, and the same ending also appears on the architectural word, which is why the two look identical.
intro.cn: ionic 是名词加希腊形容词词尾，同一个词尾也出现在建筑那个词上，因此两者看起来一模一样。

latinIntro.en: Latin took Greek ion as a loanword and added -icus, so the Latin entries here are Greek borrowings rather than native Latin nouns.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语把希腊语 ion 作为借词接收，再加上 -icus，因此这里的拉丁词条是希腊借词，而非拉丁本土名词。

items.example: The verb underlies the participle that became ion.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是后来成为 ion 的那个分词的基础。

items.structure: ion (Greek present participle, a going thing)
items.example: Faraday applied the word to particles travelling to an electrode.
items.exampleCN: 法拉第把这个词用于游向电极的粒子。

items.example: The ending turns the particle into a describing word.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把粒子变成描述性的词。

items.example: An ionic bond joins charged atoms.
items.exampleCN: 离子键把带电原子连在一起。

items.example: The flame ionizes the gas above the burner.
items.exampleCN: 火焰使燃烧器上方的气体电离。

items.example: Ionization needs energy equal to the binding of an electron.
items.exampleCN: 电离需要与电子结合能相当的能量。

items.example: An anion moves toward the anode.
A cation moves toward the cathode.

items.meaning: the Greek region on the coast of Asia Minor
items.meaningCN: 小亚细亚沿岸的希腊地区
items.example: The architectural sense comes from this place name.

latinEntries.structure: ion, iontis (n., Greek loan in Latin)

definition_zh: 归纳；归纳法；就职（入伍）典礼；感应；诱导
definition_en: reasoning from particular cases to a general rule, or the act of bringing someone or something into a role, a body or a state
core_image: 桌上排着一列深浅不同的样本，研究员从最浅的一支开始记录，最后在纸页顶端写下一条通则
scene: 实验室的桌上摆着一排颜色深浅不一的溶液，研究员从最浅的开始逐一记录，再把共同点写到本子上。 Induction begins with many small observations and ends with one general rule.
sceneCN: 这里 induction 指「从许多个别事例推出通则」（第 1 个义项：归纳推理）；句意为归纳从许多细小的观察开始，最后得到一个通则。

pos.zh: 归纳；归纳法；就职典礼；入伍；感应；诱导（多数义项不可数）

derivatives.zh: 引起；诱导；劝说（拉丁动词「引入」进入英语，由「领进来」转为「使发生」）
使正式就职；征召入伍（同一拉丁分词的另一条进入路径）
归纳的；感应的（名词词干加形容词后缀）
以归纳方式（形容词加副词后缀）

senses.title: Reasoning from particular cases
senses.definition: the move from a number of observed instances to a general statement about all such cases
senses.definitionCN: 从若干被观察的实例走向关于所有同类情形的概括陈述
senses.example: Induction begins with many small observations and ends with one general rule.
senses.exampleCN: 归纳从许多细小的观察开始，最后得到一个通则。
senses.why: The Latin verb means 'to lead in', so the mind is led from scattered cases into one rule.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词意为「领进来」，心智被从零散事例领进一条规则。

senses.title: The method itself
senses.definition: the systematic procedure of collecting cases and generalizing from them
senses.definitionCN: 收集事例并从中概括的系统程序
senses.example: Bacon urged induction as a corrective to inherited opinion.
senses.exampleCN: 培根主张以归纳法纠正沿袭的成见。
senses.why: A single move becomes a repeatable procedure with rules of its own.
senses.whyCN: 单次动作变成了有自身规则、可重复的程序。

senses.title: A ceremony of taking office
senses.definition: the formal occasion on which a person is installed in a position
senses.definitionCN: 正式使某人进入某个职位的场合
senses.example: The new rector's induction filled the hall.
senses.exampleCN: 新校长的就职典礼坐满了礼堂。
senses.why: The old sense of leading someone in survives socially: a person is led into a chair.
senses.whyCN: 「把某人领进来」的古义在社会场合留存：一个人被领进一个位子。

senses.title: Admission into an organization
senses.definition: the process of bringing a recruit or member formally into a group
senses.definitionCN: 正式把新成员引入某个群体的过程
senses.example: Induction into the unit took two weeks of training.
senses.exampleCN: 加入该部队的入门训练花了两周。
senses.why: Institutions literalize the image: a body is brought inside a gate and a set of rules.
senses.whyCN: 机构把这个意象字面化：一个人被带进一道门与一套规则之内。

senses.title: Electromagnetic induction
senses.definition: the production of a current in a conductor by a changing magnetic field
senses.definitionCN: 变化的磁场在导体中产生电流
senses.example: Faraday's induction made the electric motor possible.
senses.exampleCN: 法拉第的电磁感应使电动机成为可能。
senses.why: Nothing is physically led in; a state is induced in a nearby body without contact.
senses.whyCN: 并没有东西被实际领入；一种状态在不接触的情况下被引发于邻近物体。

senses.title: Induction of anaesthesia
senses.definition: the process of bringing a patient into anaesthesia
senses.definitionCN: 使病人进入麻醉状态的过程
senses.example: Induction takes about two minutes in adults.
senses.exampleCN: 成人的麻醉诱导约需两分钟。
senses.why: Medicine keeps the metaphor of leading a person into a state.
senses.whyCN: 医学保留了「把一个人领进某种状态」的比喻。

senses.title: Biological induction
senses.definition: the triggering of gene activity or tissue development by a signal
senses.definitionCN: 由信号触发基因活动或组织发育
senses.example: Induction of the gene followed the hormone signal.
senses.exampleCN: 该基因的诱导随激素信号而来。
senses.why: A signal from outside switches on a programme inside, which is the same leading-in at cellular scale.
senses.whyCN: 外部信号开启内部程序，这是细胞尺度上的同一种「引入」。

senses.title: The conclusion reached
senses.definition: the general statement produced by the procedure, viewed as its output
senses.definitionCN: 由该程序产生、被当作其产物的一般陈述
senses.example: The induction held until a single counter-example appeared.
senses.exampleCN: 这个归纳结论一直成立，直到出现一个反例。
senses.why: The movement of thought leaves a product behind, and the word can name that product too.
senses.whyCN: 思维的运动留下产物，这个词也能指那个产物。

intro.en: Induction comes from a Latin noun of action built on a verb meaning 'to lead in'. The logical sense grew out of the physical one.
intro.cn: induction 来自拉丁语的表动作名词，它建立在一个意为「领进来」的动词上。逻辑义是从物理义生长出来的。

items.en: Ducere meant 'to lead, draw, conduct'. It is one of the most productive verbs in the Latin vocabulary and supplies a large English family.
items.cn: ducere 意为「引领、拉、导」。它是拉丁语中构词能力最强的动词之一，提供了大批英语词。

items.en: The compound meant 'to lead or bring in', and also 'to introduce, to persuade'. The two shades have stayed together ever since.
items.cn: 这个复合词意为「引入、带进」，也指「介绍、劝说」。这两层意思此后一直并存。

items.en: The noun of action covered both a physical bringing in and, in later Latin, an argument that leads the mind to a conclusion.
items.cn: 这个表动作名词既涵盖物理上的引入，也在后来的拉丁语中指把心智引向结论的论证。

items.en: English took the noun in the fifteenth century; by the sixteenth it named the ceremony of installing a person in office.
items.cn: 英语在 15 世纪接受了这个名词；到 16 世纪它指使某人就职的典礼。

items.en: The method of generalizing from observed cases was promoted as a corrective to inherited reasoning, and the word became its standard name.
items.cn: 从观察事例概括的方法被提倡为对沿袭推理的纠正，这个词成了它的标准名称。

items.en: Nineteenth-century physics used the word for a current produced without contact, and medicine used it for bringing a patient into anaesthesia.
items.cn: 19 世纪的物理学用这个词指不接触而产生的电流，医学用同词指使病人进入麻醉。

note.en: The first group holds words built on the same leading-in verb that are constantly confused; the second holds near neighbours in reasoning.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「引入」动词、常被混淆的词；第二组是推理领域里的近义词。

entries.definition: Same Latin verb: to cause a state, to persuade, or to bring on labour; it is the everyday verb behind the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 同一拉丁动词：指使某种状态发生、劝说，或引产；是这个名词背后的日常动词。

entries.definition: Structurally the same verb but used for formal installation into a post, and for admission into military service.
entries.definitionCN: 结构上同源，但专用于正式使就职，以及征召入伍。

entries.definition: From the same leading verb with a prefix meaning 'down or away': it moves from general rules to particular cases.
entries.definitionCN: 同一「引领」动词加意为「向下、离开」的前缀：从通则走向个别情形。

entries.definition: The property of a circuit that opposes a change of current; it shares the electrical sense but names a measurement, not a process.
entries.definitionCN: 电路阻碍电流变化的性质；共享「电」这一义，但指一个量而非过程。

entries.definition: The broad statement produced by induction, stated as a result rather than as a method.
entries.definitionCN: 由归纳产生的宽泛陈述，被表述为结果而非方法。

entries.definition: Any move from evidence to conclusion, covering both the inductive and the deductive road.
entries.definitionCN: 从证据到结论的任何推进，涵盖归纳与演绎两条路。

entries.definition: It generalizes from samples to a quantity, where induction generalizes to a rule.
entries.definitionCN: 从样本概括到一个数量，而归纳概括到一条规则。

entries.definition: A transparent phrase for the ceremony sense, with no Latin root at all.
entries.definitionCN: 就职典礼义的大白话说法，完全不带拉丁词根。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The Latin verb means 'lead in', so induction leads the mind from cases into a rule.
normal.cn: 拉丁动词意为「领进来」，所以归纳把心智从事例领进一条规则。

normal.en: The family runs induce, induct, induction, inductive, inductively.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 induce、induct、induction、inductive、inductively。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the domains: induction from examples, induction ceremony, electromagnetic induction.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：由例证归纳、就职典礼、电磁感应。

normal.en: The same leading verb, with a few other prefixes, gives conduct, produce, reduce and deduce.
normal.cn: 同一个「引领」动词配上别的前缀，就得到 conduct、produce、reduce、deduce。

normal.en: Philosophy knows it as the problem of induction: no number of cases can guarantee the rule.
normal.cn: 哲学把它称作归纳问题：再多事例也无法保证那条规则。

abstract.en: Picture a hand drawing one line through a hundred scattered dots.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手在一百个散点上画出一条线。

abstract.en: Picture a door held open while someone is walked through it.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门被扶着敞开，有人正被领过去。

abstract.en: Picture a magnet moving near a wire, and the wire answering without being touched.
abstract.cn: 想象一块磁铁在导线旁移动，导线没被碰却有了回应。

examples.en: Induction from a handful of cases is useful but never certain.
examples.cn: 从少数事例归纳有用，但从不保证确定。

examples.en: The induction of new staff includes a week of shadowing.
examples.cn: 新员工的入职引导包括一周的跟岗。

examples.en: The coil produces a current by induction when the field changes.
examples.cn: 磁场变化时，线圈通过感应产生电流。

dict_mnemonic.text: in（向内）+ duct（引导）＝ 把心智从一个个事例领进一条通则 → 归纳；也指把人领进职位或某种状态。

root: 拉丁 inductio「引入」，来自 inducere「领进来、引入」，由 in-「向内」+ ducere「引领」构成。同族有 induce、induct、deduce、conduct、produce、reduce。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one leading-in. The mind can be led from cases to a rule, the procedure can be made a method, a person can be led into an office or a unit, a state can be led into a body or a circuit, and the rule itself can be the thing left behind.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一次「领进来」展开。心智可以被从事例领进一条规则，程序可以被做成方法，一个人可以被领进职位或队伍，某种状态可以被引入身体或电路，而那条规则本身也可以是留下的东西。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand leading someone through a doorway into a place they were not in before.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手领着某人穿过门口，进入他原本不在的地方。

branches.en: THE MOVE AND WHAT IT LEAVES: the leading-in of the mind, and the general statement that remains afterwards.
branches.cn: 这次引领与它留下的东西：把心智领进去，以及之后留下的那句概括。

branches.en: MADE INTO A PROCEDURE: one move repeated by rule becomes a method with a name.
branches.cn: 变成程序：一次动作按规则重复，就成了有名称的方法。

branches.en: PEOPLE LED THROUGH DOORS: into an office by ceremony, into a unit by training.
branches.cn: 被领过门的人：以典礼领进职位，以训练领进队伍。

branches.en: LED WITHOUT CONTACT: physics keeps only the effect, a state induced at a distance.
branches.cn: 不接触的引领：物理学只保留效果，即在远处被引发的状态。

branches.en: LED INTO A STATE: a patient into sleep, a cell into a switched-on programme.
branches.cn: 被领进某种状态：病人进入麻醉，细胞进入被开启的程序。

intro.en: Induction is a prefix plus a verb plus a noun ending, and each piece can be read separately.
intro.cn: induction 由前缀、动词与名词词尾构成，每一块都可以单独读出。

latinIntro.en: The leading verb with different prefixes builds a whole set of English verbs, so the family is unusually easy to read.
latinIntro.cn: 这个「引领」动词配上不同前缀，造出一整组英语动词，因此这个词族读起来格外容易。

items.example: The prefix marks movement toward an inside.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀标出朝内部去的运动。

items.structure: ducere, duxi, ductum (Latin verb, third conjugation)
items.example: The root supplies the pulling hand.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供那只牵引的手。

items.example: The compound adds direction to the pulling.
items.exampleCN: 复合词在牵引之上加了方向。

items.example: The ending turns the verb into an event.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把动词变成一个事件。

items.example: Induction led the mind from cases to a rule.
items.exampleCN: 归纳把心智从事例引向规则。

items.structure: induce (English verb from the Latin form)
items.example: The drug induces sleep within minutes.
items.exampleCN: 这种药几分钟内引起睡意。

items.structure: induct (English verb from the Latin participle)
items.example: They inducted her into the academy.
items.exampleCN: 他们正式接纳她进入学会。

items.example: An inductive step moves from cases to a rule.
items.exampleCN: 归纳的一步从事例走向规则。

items.example: The same verb with another prefix leads a group.
items.exampleCN: 同一动词配另一个前缀，就是引领一群人。

items.example: The prefix reverses the direction of travel.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把行进方向反过来。

derivatives.zh: 引起；诱导；劝说（拉丁动词「引入」进入英语，由「领进来」转为「使发生」）
使正式就职；征召入伍（同一拉丁分词的另一条进入路径）
归纳的；感应的（名词词干加形容词后缀）
以归纳方式（形容词加副词后缀）

definition_zh: 领导角色；领导职位以及该职位应有的职责与行为期待
definition_en: the position of leading a group together with the duties and behaviour that the position is expected to involve
core_image: 舞台侧面挂着一件写有职务的外套，谁穿上它，谁就要按戏里的方式说话和行动
scene: 排练前，导演把一件写着职务的外套递给替补演员，让他按主角的方式走位。 She accepted the leadership role after the board vote.
sceneCN: 这里指「正式承担的领导职位」（第 1 个义项：正式领导职位）；句意为董事会投票之后，她接受了这个领导职位。可辨识物件：外套、舞台侧幕、剧本、走位标记、座椅。

pos.zh: 领导角色（职位与职责，常作可数）
领导角色（行为期待，可数或不可数）

collocations.phrase: a leadership role in the project

senses.title: The formal position of leading
senses.definition: an official post in which a person is responsible for directing a group
senses.definitionCN: 一个人负责指导群体的正式职位
senses.example: She accepted the leadership role after the board vote.
senses.exampleCN: 董事会投票之后，她接受了这个领导职位。
senses.why: A role is a part written for whoever occupies it; a leadership role is the part that carries authority.
senses.whyCN: 角色是为占据它的人写好的戏份；领导角色就是带有权威的那份戏份。

senses.title: What others expect of the leader
senses.titleCN: 他人对领导者的行为期待
senses.definition: the set of behaviours that a group expects from the person in the leading position
senses.definitionCN: 一个群体期待处于领导位置的人做出的那套行为
senses.example: The leadership role requires listening as much as deciding.
senses.exampleCN: 领导角色要求倾听与作决定同样多。
senses.why: Every part comes with a script, and the group writes much of that script before anyone is cast.
senses.whyCN: 每个角色都带着剧本，而群体在选定人选之前就已经写好了其中大部分。

senses.title: The part someone steps into
senses.titleCN: 某人临时承担的领导角色
senses.definition: a leading part taken on in a particular situation, often without a formal title
senses.definitionCN: 在特定情境中承担的领导角色，往往没有正式头衔
senses.example: In the rescue, a quiet volunteer took the leadership role.
senses.exampleCN: 在救援中，一位安静的志愿者承担了领导角色。
senses.why: When a situation needs someone to give cues, a person can step into the part even without the office.
senses.whyCN: 当情境需要有人发出提示时，即使没有职位，人也可以踏进这个角色。

senses.title: The rotating part in a team
senses.titleCN: 团队中轮换的领导角色
senses.definition: a leading function assigned to a team member for a period and then passed on
senses.definitionCN: 在某一时期内分配给团队成员、随后转交他人的领导职能
senses.example: Each project team rotates its leadership role every term.
senses.exampleCN: 每个项目团队每学期轮换一次领导角色。
senses.why: If a role is a part rather than a person, it can be handed from one player to another without breaking the play.
senses.whyCN: 如果角色是戏份而非人，它就可以从一个演员交给另一个，而戏不会中断。

senses.title: The part held across a long project
senses.titleCN: 长期项目中持续承担的领导角色
senses.definition: responsibility for directing a multi-stage piece of work from start to finish
senses.definitionCN: 从开始到结束指导一项多阶段工作的责任
senses.example: His leadership role on the bridge project lasted three years.
senses.exampleCN: 他在桥梁项目中的领导角色持续了三年。
senses.why: Long work needs a continuous part, not a single cue; the role becomes a thread through the schedule.
senses.whyCN: 长期工作需要持续的角色，而非一次提示；这个角色于是贯穿整个日程。

senses.title: The part recognized by a community
senses.titleCN: 共同体认可的领导角色
senses.definition: an informal leading position granted by a community's trust rather than by an appointment
senses.definitionCN: 由共同体信任而非任命授予的非正式领导位置
senses.example: The elder's leadership role in the village was never written down.
senses.exampleCN: 这位长者在村庄里的领导角色从未被写下来。
senses.why: Some roles are written on paper and some on memory; a community can cast a part without a document.
senses.whyCN: 有些角色写在纸上，有些写在记忆里；共同体可以在没有文件的情况下分配角色。

senses.title: The part demanded by a crisis
senses.definition: the specific leading behaviour required when a group faces urgent danger or uncertainty
senses.definitionCN: 群体面对紧急危险或不确定时所需的特定领导行为
senses.example: A crisis leadership role demands clear public communication.
senses.exampleCN: 危机中的领导角色要求清晰的公共沟通。
senses.why: A crisis rewrites the script overnight and asks the person in the part to speak plainly and quickly.
senses.whyCN: 危机会在一夜之间改写剧本，要求承担角色的人说得清楚、说得及时。

senses.title: One part shared by several people
senses.titleCN: 由数人共同担任的领导角色
senses.definition: a leading function divided among two or more people instead of held by a single chair
senses.definitionCN: 由两人或更多人分担、而非由单一主席持有的领导职能
senses.example: The cooperative uses a shared leadership role instead of a single chair.
senses.exampleCN: 这家合作社采用共享的领导角色，而不是单一主席。
senses.why: If the part can be written, it can also be split, so that no single actor carries every line.
senses.whyCN: 既然角色可以被写出来，它也可以被拆开，使没有任何一个演员承担全部台词。

intro.en: Leadership role joins leadership, from Old English lǣdan 'to lead', with role, from French rôle 'a roll of paper, a part', from Latin rotulus 'small scroll', a diminutive of rota 'wheel'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: leadership role 由 leadership 与 role 组合而成。leadership 出自古英语 lǣdan「带领」；role 来自法语 rôle「纸卷、角色」，再往上出自拉丁 rotulus「小卷轴」，是 rota「轮子」的指小形式。年代均为约数。

items.en: Lǣdan meant 'to lead, guide', a causative form related to līþan 'to go'. Its pre-Germanic source is reconstructed.
items.cn: lǣdan 意为「带领、引导」，是与 līþan「行走」相关的使役形式。它在日耳曼语之前的来源属于重构。

items.en: Leadership was formed from leader plus the state suffix -ship, naming the condition or activity of leading.
items.cn: leadership 由 leader 加表示状态的名词后缀构成，指领导的状态或活动。

items.en: Rota meant 'wheel'. Its deeper origin is not established; the wheel root proposed for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: rota 意为「轮子」。其更深来源未得到证明；为它提出的「轮」词根属于重构形式。

items.en: The diminutive rotulus named a small wheel and then a rolled scroll of paper.
items.cn: 指小形式 rotulus 先指小轮，后指卷起的纸卷。

items.en: French rôle named the roll on which an actor's part was written, and English adopted it for the part itself.
items.cn: 法语 rôle 指写下演员台词的那卷纸，英语借用来指角色本身。

items.en: The compound leadership role appeared in twentieth-century management writing, where a post is described as a part with expectations attached.
items.cn: 这个复合短语出现在二十世纪的管理写作中，把职位描述为一个附带行为期待的角色。

note.en: Group one holds the two components and their relatives; group two holds words for a post and its duties.
note.cn: 第一组是两个构词成分及其亲属词；第二组是表示职位及其职责的词。

entries.definition: The ability or body of leaders; the phrase narrows it to one specific part.
entries.definitionCN: 领导能力或领导层；这个短语把它收窄为某一个具体角色。

entries.definition: A part played or a function performed; alone it can describe an actor as easily as a manager.
entries.definitionCN: 扮演的角色或承担的职能；单独使用时既可指演员，也可指管理者。

entries.definition: The individual who fills the role; the phrase names the part, not the person.
entries.definitionCN: 填补这个角色的个人；这个短语命名的是角色，而非人。

entries.definition: The main part in a play or film; it looks similar but belongs to casting rather than management.
entries.definitionCN: 戏剧或电影中的主角；看起来相似，却属于选角而非管理。

entries.definition: A job or office in an organization; it names the slot rather than the behaviour expected in it.
entries.definitionCN: 组织中的职位或岗位；指位置本身，而非对该位置的行为期待。

entries.definition: The purpose or duty that a person or office is meant to perform.
entries.definitionCN: 一个人或职位应当履行的目的或职责。

entries.definition: An official instruction or authority given to someone; a role can exist without a formal mandate.
entries.definitionCN: 授予某人的官方指示或权限；角色可以在没有正式授权的情况下存在。

entries.definition: The act of choosing someone for a post; it is the casting decision, not the part itself.
entries.definitionCN: 选择某人担任职位的行为；这是选角决定，而非角色本身。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real walking root, the real scroll image behind role and the real management phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的「行走」词根、role 背后真实的纸卷意象与真实的管理搭配。

normal.en: The first word means the activity of leading; the second began as a paper roll holding an actor's lines, so the phrase means the part written for a leader.
normal.cn: 第一个词指领导活动；第二个词原指写有演员台词的纸卷，因此整个短语意为「为领导者写好的那份戏份」。

normal.en: The family runs leadership, leader, lead, role, role-play and role model.
normal.cn: 同族词包括领导、领导者、带领、角色、角色扮演与角色榜样。

normal.en: The management phrases are take on a leadership role, assume a leadership role and step into a leadership role.
normal.cn: 管理搭配有承担领导角色、就任领导职位与走上领导岗位。

normal.en: The descriptive phrases are shared leadership role and leadership role expectations.
normal.cn: 描述性搭配有共享的领导角色与对领导角色的期待。

normal.en: The same scroll root appears in the word for a part in a play, which still means a scripted role.
normal.cn: 同一「纸卷」词根出现在表示戏剧角色的词中，那个词至今仍指写好的角色。

abstract.en: Picture a coat hanging at the side of a stage, with a name written on its collar.
abstract.cn: 想象舞台侧边挂着一件外套，衣领上写着名字。

abstract.en: Picture a paper roll handed to an understudy, already full of lines he did not write.
abstract.cn: 想象一卷纸递给替补演员，上面早已写满他没写过的台词。

abstract.en: Picture two people holding the same coat at once, each carrying half the lines.
abstract.cn: 想象两个人同时拿着同一件外套，每人念一半台词。

examples.en: The leadership role comes with responsibility for the budget as well as the staff.
examples.cn: 这个领导角色既带来对员工的责任，也带来对预算的责任。

examples.en: She stepped into a leadership role when the director resigned.
examples.cn: 主任辞职后，她走上了领导岗位。

examples.en: The study asked how leadership roles are shared in small cooperatives.
examples.cn: 这项研究追问小型合作社如何分担领导角色。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「领导」加「角色」——穿上这件写着职务的外套，就要按戏里的方式说话 → 领导角色、领导职位

root: leadership role 由 leadership 与 role 组合而成。leadership 出自古英语 lǣdan「带领」；role 来自法语 rôle「纸卷、角色」，再往上出自拉丁 rotulus「小卷轴」，是 rota「轮子」的指小形式。rota 的更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one theatrical image: a part is written, cast, stepped into, rotated, held for years, recognized by an audience, rewritten in a crisis and sometimes shared by two actors.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个戏剧意象展开：一份戏份被写好、被分配、被踏进去、被轮换、被长期持有、被观众认可、在危机中被改写，有时还由两名演员共同承担。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a costume hanging at the side of a stage.
core.cn: 核心意象：舞台侧边挂着的一件戏服。

branches.en: THE CAST PART: a formal post is a role assigned to one person by decision.
branches.cn: 被分配的角色：正式职位是通过决定分配给某个人的角色。

branches.en: THE SCRIPT: expectations and crisis conditions both tell the actor which lines to say.
branches.cn: 剧本：行为期待与危机情境都在告诉演员该念哪些台词。

branches.en: THE UNDERSTUDY: someone steps into the part when the situation calls for it.
branches.cn: 替补上场：情境需要时，有人踏进这个角色。

branches.en: THE SHARED PART: the role can rotate or be split so that no single actor owns it.
branches.cn: 共享角色：角色可以轮换或拆开，使任何单个演员都无法独占。

branches.en: THE LONG RUN: a project part lasts for years, and a community part is remembered without a document.
branches.cn: 长期上演：项目角色持续多年，共同体角色则无需文件也被记住。

intro.en: The phrase can be read from an Old English verb of leading and a Latin noun for a scroll that became the word for a part.
intro.cn: 这个短语可以按表示带领的古英语动词，以及由拉丁语「卷轴」演变而来、后来表示角色的名词逐段读出。

latinIntro.en: The first element is native English; the second came through French from Latin rotulus, a small scroll, and rota, a wheel.
latinIntro.cn: 第一个成分是英语本族词；第二个成分经法语来自拉丁 rotulus「小卷轴」与 rota「轮子」。

items.example: The verb supplies the leading half of the phrase.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供短语中「领导」的一半。

items.meaning: the activity or role of leading
items.example: Leadership was shared between two offices.
items.exampleCN: 领导职责由两个办公室分担。

items.example: The noun named a round object.

items.meaning: small wheel; a roll of paper
items.example: The scroll was a rotulus before it was a role.
items.exampleCN: 在成为角色之前，它是一卷纸。

items.example: The part was written on a roll.
Every member has a role in the drill.
items.exampleCN: 每个人在演练中都有角色。
班级进行了一场谈判的角色扮演。

items.meaning: a person whose behaviour others imitate
items.example: The coach served as a role model for the team.
items.exampleCN: 教练成为团队的行为榜样。

items.meaning: the part assigned to a leader
items.example: She took the leadership role in the campaign.
items.exampleCN: 她在活动中承担了领导角色。

definition_zh: 生物碱；（尤指植物中的）含氮碱性有机化合物
definition_en: a nitrogen-containing organic compound of plant origin that usually has marked physiological action on the body
core_image: 藏在植物里的苦味药性分子：一口咬下去又苦又冲
scene: 药学课上老师切开一种有毒的植物果实。 The scientist extracted a bitter alkaloid from the plant.
sceneCN: 这里的 alkaloid 是「生物碱」（第 1 个义项：从植物中提取的含氮碱性化合物）；句意是科学家从植物中提取出一种苦味的生物碱。

pos.zh: 生物碱；含氮碱性有机化合物

derivatives.zh: 同族形容词，义为「碱性的」，与 alkali 相关
同族名词，义为「碱」，是 alkaloid 的直接来源
由 alkali 加动词后缀构成，义为「碱化」

senses.title: A nitrogenous plant compound with drug-like action
senses.titleCN: 生物碱：植物含氮碱性化合物
senses.definition: an organic, nitrogen-containing compound made by plants that strongly affects animal bodies
senses.definitionCN: 植物产生的含氮有机化合物，对动物机体有强烈作用
senses.example: Morphine is an alkaloid obtained from the opium poppy.
senses.exampleCN: 吗啡是从罂粟中提取的一种生物碱。
senses.why: The word is built on alkali plus -oid, so the core image is an alkali-like substance hiding in plants.
senses.whyCN: 这个词由 alkali（碱）加 -oid（类似物）构成，核心意象是藏在植物里的类似碱的物质。

senses.title: Any synthetic compound resembling plant alkaloids
senses.titleCN: 类生物碱：人工合成的相似化合物
senses.definition: a synthetic or semisynthetic compound whose structure or action resembles natural plant alkaloids
senses.definitionCN: 结构或作用类似天然植物生物碱的合成或半合成化合物
senses.example: The lab produced a synthetic alkaloid for pain relief.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室合成了一种用于镇痛的类生物碱。
senses.why: Once the natural class was named, chemistry extended -oid to any look-alike compound.
senses.whyCN: 天然类别命名后，化学界把 -oid（类似）扩展到任何外观相似的化合物上。

senses.title: Alkaloids collectively as a class
senses.titleCN: 生物碱类：作为整体类别
senses.definition: alkaloids considered collectively as a chemical family in pharmacology
senses.definitionCN: 药理学中作为一族化学物质被整体谈论的生物碱
senses.example: This family of alkaloids affects the nervous system.
senses.exampleCN: 这一族生物碱作用于神经系统。
senses.why: A mass sense arises when chemists talk about the family rather than one compound.
senses.whyCN: 当化学家谈论整个家族而非单个化合物时，就产生了不可数的类指义项。

senses.title: A specific alkaloid molecule identified in analysis
senses.definition: a particular alkaloid identified or measured in chemical analysis
senses.definitionCN: 化学分析中被鉴定或测出的某一种生物碱
senses.example: Each alkaloid was separated by chromatography.
senses.exampleCN: 每种生物碱都通过色谱法被分离出来。
senses.why: The countable sense lets researchers point at one molecule within the family.
senses.whyCN: 可数义项让研究者能指向家族中的某一个分子。

senses.title: A poisonous principle in toxicology
senses.definition: an alkaloid regarded as the toxic principle of a poisonous plant
senses.definitionCN: 被视为有毒植物毒性来源的生物碱成分
senses.example: The poison actsonally through its alkaloid.
senses.exampleCN: 这种毒物实际上是靠其中的生物碱起作用的。
senses.why: Because many alkaloids are bitter and toxic, toxicology singles them out as the active poison.
senses.whyCN: 许多生物碱苦而有毒，毒理学因此把它们单独看作起效的毒物成分。

senses.title: An alkaloid used as medicine
senses.definition: an alkaloid used as a pharmacologically active ingredient in drugs
senses.definitionCN: 用作药物中有效成分的生物碱
senses.example: Doctors prescribed an alkaloid to lower blood pressure.
senses.exampleCN: 医生开了一种降压的生物碱类药物。
senses.why: The same strong action that makes alkaloids toxic makes them valuable medicines.
senses.whyCN: 让生物碱有毒的那种强烈作用，也正是它们能入药的原因。

senses.title: Alkaloid content of a material
senses.definition: the amount of alkaloids present in a plant or product, measured as a proportion
senses.definitionCN: 植物或产品中所含生物碱的量，以比例计
senses.example: This variety has a high alkaloid content.
senses.exampleCN: 这个品种的生物碱含量很高。
senses.why: In agriculture and industry the word shifts from naming a molecule to naming an amount.
senses.whyCN: 在农业和工业语境中，这个词从指称分子转为指称含量。

senses.title: A marker for plant classification
senses.definition: the alkaloid profile of a plant used to identify or classify the species
senses.definitionCN: 用于鉴定或分类物种的植物生物碱谱
senses.example: Researchers compared the alkaloid profile of two related species.
senses.exampleCN: 研究者比较了两个近缘种的生物碱谱。
senses.why: Because each species makes its own alkaloid mixture, the mixture becomes a fingerprint.
senses.whyCN: 每个物种产生自己独特的生物碱混合物，这种混合物就成了指纹。

intro.en: Alkaloid combines alkali with the adjective suffix -oid, coined in early nineteenth-century chemistry.
intro.cn: alkaloid 由 alkali（碱）加形容词后缀 -oid（类似……的）构成，是十九世纪早期化学的造词。

items.en: al-qalya, "the ashes of saltwort", the source of alkali.
items.cn: 阿拉伯语 al-qalya「盐蓬草的灰烬」，是 alkali 的来源。

items.en: alkali, borrowed from Arabic for the caustic ash substance.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 alkali，借自阿拉伯语，指苛性灰质。

items.en: -oides, "like, resembling", adapted into Latin as -oid.
items.cn: 希腊语 -oides「类似」，经拉丁语转为 -oid。

items.en: German Chemists formed Alkaloid for the alkali-like plant bases.
items.cn: 十九世纪一二十年代德国化学家造 Alkaloid 一词指碱性的植物碱类。

items.en: English alkaloid appears in chemical writing soon after.
items.cn: 英语 alkaloid 随后在化学文献中出现。

items.en: Now the standard pharmacological term for nitrogenous plant bases.
items.cn: 如今是药理学中含氮植物碱的标准术语。

note.en: Distinguish alkaloid from its sibling words alkali and alkaline, and from look-alike chemistry terms.
note.cn: 要把 alkaloid 与同族词 alkali、alkaline 区分开，也要与拼写相近的化学词区分。

entries.definition: a soluble base such as lye; the parent word of alkaloid.
entries.definitionCN: 碱（如碱液）；alkaloid 的来源词。

entries.definition: adjective meaning containing or like an alkali.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词「碱性的」，与 alkali 同根。

entries.definition: a different class of organic compounds; shares the Arabic al- article but not the root.
entries.definitionCN: 另一类有机化合物；同样带有阿拉伯语冠词 al-，但词根不同，只是形近。

entries.definition: another class of plant-derived bioactive compounds, built on sugars.
entries.definitionCN: 另一类植物来源的活性化合物，以糖为骨架。

entries.definition: a bitter plant compound that precipitates proteins.
entries.definitionCN: 使蛋白质沉淀的苦味植物化合物。

entries.definition: any poisonous substance, of which some alkaloids are examples.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指有毒物质，部分生物碱属于毒素。

normalIntro.en: Remember alkaloid through its two building blocks.
normalIntro.cn: 通过两个构件记住 alkaloid。

normal.en: alkali + -oid: an alkali-like substance.
normal.cn: alkali（碱）+ -oid（类似物）：像碱一样的物质。

normal.en: al-qalya was the ash of saltwort plants — alkaloids often come from plants too.
normal.cn: al-qalya 原指盐蓬草灰烬——生物碱也常来自植物。

normal.en: Family chain: alkali → alkaline → alkaloid, from base to adjective to plant molecule.
normal.cn: 词族链条：alkali → alkaline → alkaloid，从碱到形容词再到植物分子。

normal.en: Most alkaloids are bitter — think of the -oid ending as "the bitter look-alike".
normal.cn: 多数生物碱是苦的——把 -oid 想成「苦味的类似物」。

normal.en: Morphine, caffeine, nicotine: famous -oid-less members, all alkaloids.
normal.cn: 吗啡、咖啡因、尼古丁：虽然没有 -oid 结尾，都是著名生物碱。

abstract.en: Picture a green leaf hiding a tiny crystal of "plant alkali".
abstract.cn: 想象一片绿叶里藏着一粒「植物碱」的小晶体。

abstract.en: The bitter taste on your tongue is the molecule announcing itself.
abstract.cn: 舌尖的苦味就是分子在自我通报。

abstract.en: A chemist ladles ash from a plant fire and pulls out a white powder.
abstract.cn: 化学家从烧尽的植物灰里舀出一勺白色粉末。

examples.en: Caffeine is the best-known alkaloid in tea and coffee.
examples.cn: 咖啡因是茶和咖啡中最著名的生物碱。

examples.en: The alkaloid content of the herb makes it toxic to livestock.
examples.cn: 这种草药的生物碱含量使它对牲畜有毒。

examples.en: Chemists isolated a new alkaloid from the rainforest vine.
examples.cn: 化学家从雨林藤蔓中分离出一种新的生物碱。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「奥克劳德」——想想“苦味的老克劳德”，他像碱一样冲口，是从植物里熬出来的老药汤。

root: 阿拉伯语 al-qalya（盐蓬草的灰烬，制碱原料）经中世纪拉丁语 alkali 进入英语，十九世纪化学家加上希腊语来源的 -oid（类似）构成 alkaloid，字面义为「类似碱的物质」。

sensesIntro.en: From the basic chemical class, the senses widen to synthetic look-alikes, the family as a whole, single molecules, and then to poison, medicine, content, and classification.
sensesIntro.cn: 从基本的化学类别出发，义项扩展到合成的类似物、作为整体的家族、单个分子，再到毒物、药物、含量和分类用途。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bitter alkali-like molecule hidden in plants
core.cn: 核心意象：藏在植物里的苦味类碱分子

branches.en: The basic nitrogenous plant compound itself.
branches.cn: 基本的含氮植物化合物本身。

branches.en: Synthetic look-alikes and the family considered collectively.
branches.cn: 合成的类似物与作为整体谈论的家族。

branches.en: Single molecules, whether as poison or analyzed substance.
branches.cn: 单个分子，无论作为毒物还是分析对象。

branches.en: The same strong action turned into medicine.
branches.cn: 同样的强烈作用转化为药物。

branches.en: Content and profile as practical measures and markers.
branches.cn: 含量与谱系作为实用指标和分类标记。

intro.en: Alkaloid is transparently built from a borrowed base and a Greek-derived suffix.
intro.cn: alkaloid 由借来的词基和希腊来源的后缀清晰构成。

latinIntro.en: The root traveled from Arabic through Medieval Latin into European chemistry.
latinIntro.cn: 词根经阿拉伯语和中世纪拉丁语进入欧洲化学。

definition_en: a condition or resource that lets a firm outperform its rivals in a market
core_image: 同一场比赛里，一名选手脚下多了一双带钉的跑鞋，起跑线却没有变
scene: 两家工厂的成品并排摆在展台上，其中一家的产品更薄、更省电，价签却相同。 A durable competitive advantage usually rests on resources rivals cannot copy.
sceneCN: 这里 competitive advantage 指「企业胜过对手的有利条件」（第 1 个义项：使企业在市场中表现优于对手的条件或资源）；句意为持久的竞争优势通常建立在对手无法复制的资源上。图中可辨识物件：并排展台、更薄更省电的产品、相同价签、对手的产品。

pos.zh: 竞争优势

senses.title: A general edge over rivals
senses.definition: any condition that lets a firm serve buyers better or more cheaply than its rivals
senses.definitionCN: 使企业比对手更好或更便宜地服务买主的任何条件
