senses.example: A reliable supply chain gave the retailer a competitive advantage.
senses.exampleCN: 可靠的供应链给了这家零售商竞争优势。
senses.why: advantage comes from avant 'before', so the phrase names a position ahead of rivals rather than a fixed property.
senses.whyCN: advantage 来自 avant「在前」，因此这个短语指相对对手靠前的位置，而非固定属性。

senses.title: Cost advantage
senses.definition: the ability to produce or deliver at a lower cost than competitors
senses.definitionCN: 以低于竞争对手的成本生产或交付的能力
senses.example: Low labour costs were its original competitive advantage.
senses.exampleCN: 低劳动成本是它最初的竞争优势。
senses.why: cost is the easiest edge to measure, so the phrase often takes this narrow reading in industry reports.
senses.whyCN: 成本是最容易测量的优势，因此在产业报告中这个短语常取这一窄义。

senses.title: Differentiation advantage
senses.definition: an edge from offering something buyers value that rivals do not offer
senses.definitionCN: 通过提供买主看重而对手不提供的东西取得的优势
senses.example: Design became the brand's competitive advantage.
senses.exampleCN: 设计成了这个品牌的竞争优势。
senses.why: when price cannot be lowered further, the edge must come from a difference buyers are willing to pay for.
senses.whyCN: 当价格无法再降，优势就只能来自买主愿意为之付费的差异。

senses.title: A durable advantage
senses.definition: an edge that survives imitation and market change for a long period
senses.definitionCN: 长期经受住模仿与市场变化的优势
senses.example: A patent-protected process is a sustainable competitive advantage.
senses.exampleCN: 受专利保护的工艺是一种可持续的竞争优势。
senses.why: strategy writing added durable because most edges are copied quickly and stop being advantages.
senses.whyCN: 战略写作加上「持久」一词，因为多数优势很快被复制，就不再是优势。

senses.title: An advantage rooted in resources
senses.definition: an edge that comes from resources a firm owns that are rare and hard to imitate
senses.definitionCN: 来自企业拥有的稀缺且难以模仿的资源
senses.example: Rare earth deposits are a resource-based competitive advantage.
senses.exampleCN: 稀土矿藏是一种基于资源的竞争优势。
senses.why: the resource-based view asks what the firm owns, not what it does, so the phrase shifts to stocks rather than actions.
senses.whyCN: 资源基础观问企业拥有什么而非做什么，因此这个短语转向「存量」而非「动作」。

senses.title: A locational advantage
senses.definition: an edge from being close to markets, suppliers, ports or skilled labour
senses.definitionCN: 因靠近市场、供应商、港口或熟练劳动力而获得的优势
senses.example: Proximity to the port is a locational competitive advantage.
senses.exampleCN: 靠近港口是一种区位竞争优势。
senses.why: advantage can attach to a place, because distance still costs money even in a digital economy.
senses.whyCN: 优势可以附着在地点上，因为即使在数字经济中，距离仍然要花钱。

senses.title: First-mover advantage
senses.definition: an edge gained by entering a market before rivals and locking in customers or standards
senses.definitionCN: 先于对手进入市场并锁定顾客或标准而取得的优势
senses.example: Being first to the market gave the startup a competitive advantage.
senses.exampleCN: 率先进入市场给了这家初创企业竞争优势。
senses.why: the phrase covers timing as well as resources, since an early position can itself be the asset.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语也涵盖时机，因为靠前的位置本身就可以是资产。

senses.title: An edge for any organization
senses.titleCN: 任何组织相对对手的有利条件
senses.definition: the same idea applied to a team, university or charity rather than a business
senses.definitionCN: 同一观念被用于队伍、大学或慈善机构而非企业
senses.example: A well-drilled team can turn a competitive advantage into a win.
senses.exampleCN: 训练有素的队伍能把竞争优势转化为胜利。
senses.why: once rivals are anywhere, advantage follows them beyond commercial markets.
senses.whyCN: 一旦对手无处不在，优势就跟着越出商业市场。

intro.en: Competitive comes from Latin competere 'to strive together'. Advantage comes through Old French avantage from avant 'before', ultimately from Latin ab ante 'from before'. The phrase is twentieth-century strategy vocabulary. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: competitive 来自拉丁 competere「一起力争」。advantage 经古法语 avantage 上溯 avant「在前」，最终来自拉丁 ab ante「从前面」。整个短语是 20 世纪战略词汇。年代均为约数。

items.en: The phrase ab ante meant 'from before, in front of'. Its shortened form ante 'before' is the seed of the whole advantage family.
items.cn: ab ante 意为「从前面、在……之前」，其简式 ante「在前」是整族 advantage 词的种子。

items.en: Avant 'before' plus the noun suffix -age produced avantage, a position ahead of others or a profit gained from it.
items.cn: avant「在前」加名词后缀 -age 构成 avantage，指领先于他人的位置或由此得到的利益。

items.en: English borrowed advantage in the fourteenth century, first as a favourable position, then as a benefit or profit.
items.cn: 英语在 14 世纪借入 advantage，先指有利位置，后指好处或利益。

items.en: Competere joins com- 'together' to petere 'seek'; competitive entered English as an adjective for anything able to contend.
items.cn: competere 把 com-「共同」接在 petere「寻求」上；competitive 作为形容词进入英语，形容能够相争的事物。

items.en: Competitive advantage became central to business strategy writing in the 1980s, when analysts asked why some firms consistently outperform others.
items.cn: 20 世纪 80 年代，当分析者追问为何某些企业持续胜过其他企业时，competitive advantage 成为企业战略写作的核心。

items.en: The exact first printed use of the full phrase is not recorded; earlier economics used advantage and competitive separately. The Latin and French steps are documented.
items.cn: 完整短语的最早印刷用例没有确切记录；更早的经济学写作分开使用 advantage 与 competitive。拉丁与法语环节有据可查。

note.en: Group one holds look-alike words from the advantage family, including one that is a doublet rather than a derivative; group two holds near terms for an edge that are not identical to it.
note.cn: 第一组是 advantage 词族中易混的词，其中一个是对偶词而非派生词；第二组是表示「优势」的近义说法，与它并不完全等同。

entries.definition: From the same avant 'before' line, but it means to move forward in space or time, not to hold a favourable position.
entries.definitionCN: 同出 avant「在前」这条线，但意为在空间或时间上向前移动，而非占据有利位置。

entries.definition: Dis- added to advantage in English, naming an unfavourable position; it is not a Latin word.
entries.definitionCN: dis- 在英语中加在 advantage 上，指不利位置；它不是拉丁词。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning favourable; a competitive advantage is the noun, while advantageous describes the condition.
entries.definitionCN: 表示「有利的」形容词；competitive advantage 是名词，而 advantageous 描述该条件。

entries.definition: The rival itself; an advantage exists only in relation to a competitor, but the two words name different things.
entries.definitionCN: 指对手本身；优势只在与竞争者相对时存在，但这两个词指称不同事物。

entries.definition: A small lead or sharpness over rivals; it is the everyday word for what competitive advantage states formally.
entries.definitionCN: 对对手的微小领先或锋利之处；它是竞争优势正式说法的日常版本。

entries.definition: A capability a firm possesses; a strength becomes an advantage only when buyers or rivals make it valuable.
entries.definitionCN: 企业拥有的能力；只有当买主或对手使其有价值时，能力才成为优势。

entries.definition: A resource with value; assets can support an advantage, but an asset by itself may be neither rare nor useful.
entries.definitionCN: 有价值的资源；资产可以支撑优势，但一项资产本身未必稀缺或有用。

entries.definition: The state of being better than another; it is a verdict, while competitive advantage is a market condition.
entries.definitionCN: 优于他者的状态；它是一种评判，而竞争优势是一种市场条件。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: avant 'before' + -age: advantage is literally a position in front.
normal.cn: avant「在前」+ -age：advantage 字面上就是「靠前的位置」。

normal.en: The family runs advantage, advantageous, disadvantage, disadvantaged, competitive, competitor.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 advantage、advantageous、disadvantage、disadvantaged、competitive、competitor。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the strategy sense: sustainable competitive advantage, source of competitive advantage.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出战略义：可持续竞争优势、竞争优势的来源。

normal.en: Strategy writing pairs it with three sources: cost, differentiation and focus.
normal.cn: 战略写作把它与三种来源配对：成本、差异化与聚焦。

normal.en: The everyday twin is competitive edge, used in speech more than in reports.
normal.cn: 日常的对应说法是 competitive edge，多用于口语而非报告。

abstract.en: Picture a runner with better shoes on the same starting line.
abstract.cn: 想象一名跑者站在同一条起跑线上，脚上却是一双更好的鞋。

abstract.en: Picture two stalls side by side, one with a shorter queue.
abstract.cn: 想象并排的两个摊位，其中一个队伍更短。

abstract.en: Picture a map where one warehouse sits closer to every road.
abstract.cn: 想象一张地图，其中一座仓库离每条路都更近。

examples.en: The firm's competitive advantage disappeared once the patent expired.
examples.cn: 专利一到期，这家企业的竞争优势就消失了。

examples.en: Training staff well can create a competitive advantage that rivals cannot buy.
examples.cn: 把员工培训好，可以创造对手买不到的竞争优势。

examples.en: Analysts asked which competitive advantage would survive the next price war.
examples.cn: 分析者追问哪一项竞争优势能挺过下一场价格战。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「competitive（竞争的）+ advantage（靠前的位置）」——在竞争中站得更靠前 → 竞争优势

root: competitive 来自拉丁 competere「一起力争」（com- + petere「寻求」）；advantage 经古法语 avantage 上溯 avant「在前」，最终来自拉丁 ab ante「从前面」。整个短语为 20 世纪战略用语。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one lead: a firm stands ahead of its rivals, and that lead is then located in cost, in difference, in durability, in owned resources, in a place, in timing, and finally in any organization that has rivals.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个「靠前」展开：企业站在对手前面，这个靠前再依次落在成本、差异、持久性、自有资源、地点、时机，最后落在任何有对手的组织上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a runner on the same starting line with better shoes.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一条起跑线上，一名跑者穿着更好的鞋。

branches.en: THE PLAIN LEAD: any condition that puts a firm ahead.
branches.cn: 朴素的领先：任何使企业靠前的条件。

branches.en: TWO ROUTES: charge less, or offer what rivals do not.
branches.cn: 两条路径：收得更少，或提供对手没有的东西。

branches.en: DURABILITY AND OWNERSHIP: an edge that survives imitation, and one rooted in what the firm owns.
branches.cn: 持久与所有：经得住模仿的优势，以及扎根于企业自有资源的优势。

branches.en: PLACE AND TIMING: proximity to roads and ports, and the advantage of arriving first.
branches.cn: 地点与时机：靠近道路与港口，以及先到一步的好处。

branches.en: BEYOND BUSINESS: the same lead sought by a team, a school or a charity.
branches.cn: 越出商业：队伍、学校或慈善机构追求的同一个领先。

intro.en: The phrase combines a Latin-derived adjective of striving with a French-derived noun of being in front; neither half is a bare root.
intro.cn: 这个短语把拉丁来源的「相争」形容词与法语来源的「在前」名词组合起来；两半都不是光秃的词根。

latinIntro.en: Latin petere and com- supply competitive and competitor; Latin ante, through French avant, supplies advantage, advantageous and disadvantage.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 petere 与 com- 提供 competitive 与 competitor；拉丁 ante 经法语 avant 提供 advantage、advantageous 与 disadvantage。

items.structure: Latin preposition ante (before, in front of)
items.example: The Latin word survives inside advantage and advance.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁词留在 advantage 与 advance 之中。

items.example: Height is an advantage in basketball.
The early train is advantageous for commuters.
Distance is a disadvantage for the shop.
items.exampleCN: 距离远是这家店的不利条件。
该项目服务处境不利的学生。

items.example: Four firms compete for the tender.
items.exampleCN: 四家企业争夺这项招标。
这项服务定价有竞争力。

items.example: A rival copied the design within a year.
items.exampleCN: 一家对手在一年内复制了设计。

items.example: The extra staff gave them an edge.
items.exampleCN: 多出的员工给了他们一点优势。

items.example: The land was bought advantageously before prices rose.
items.exampleCN: 这块地在涨价前被有利地买下。

definition_zh: 顾问；提供专业建议的人；（大学的）指导教师；（政府的）高级幕僚
definition_en: a person whose job is to give expert advice; a teacher who guides a student’s course choices; a senior official who advises a government
core_image: 站在你旁边、替你把眼前局面看清楚的那个人
scene: 选课表摊在桌上，学生拿不定主意，于是敲开了那扇门。 She asked her advisor which course to take first.
sceneCN: 这里 advisor 是「指导教师」（第 2 个义项：在学校里指导学生选课与学业安排的人）；句意为她问导师该先修哪门课。核心画面是有人替你把局面看清楚，再告诉你往哪走。

pos.zh: 顾问；指导教师；幕僚

collocations.phrase: on the advice of an advisor

derivatives.zh: 由同一词根构成，义为「建议；劝告」，是 advisor 所做的事
加 -ory 构成，义为「顾问的；咨询的；劝告的」
加 -able 构成，义为「明智的；可取的」
同族名词，义为「建议；忠告」，不可数

senses.title: A person paid to give expert advice
senses.definition: a person whose job is to give professional advice on money, law, business or policy
senses.definitionCN: 以提供理财、法律、商业或政策方面的专业意见为职业的人
senses.example: The company hired a financial advisor before the merger.
senses.exampleCN: 公司在并购前聘请了一位理财顾问。
senses.why: The root means to cause someone to see, so an advisor is literally the person who makes the situation visible to you.
senses.whyCN: 词根的意思是「使人看见」，所以 advisor 字面上就是那个让你看清局面的人——你看不到的风险，他替你看。

senses.title: A teacher who guides a student’s studies
senses.definition: a teacher at a school or college who helps students choose courses and plan their studies
senses.definitionCN: 在学校或大学里帮助学生选课、规划学业的教师
senses.example: My advisor suggested I take statistics in the second year.
senses.exampleCN: 我的导师建议我第二年修统计学。
senses.why: The same seeing image narrows to one field: the advisor sees the whole curriculum and points out the path a student cannot yet see.
senses.whyCN: 同一个「看清」的意象收窄到学业这一域：导师看得见整张课程地图，于是指出学生自己还看不见的那条路。

senses.title: A senior official who advises a government
senses.definition: a senior official who gives advice to a government or a head of state, often in a titled post
senses.definitionCN: 向政府或国家元首提供意见的高级官员，常带正式头衔
senses.example: He served as national security advisor for four years.
senses.exampleCN: 他担任了四年国家安全顾问。
senses.why: Here the seeing is done for a whole state: the advisor is the extra pair of eyes attached to power, which is why the spelling advisor is preferred in official titles.
senses.whyCN: 这里是替整个国家「看」：顾问是接在权力旁边的另一双眼睛，也正因这种正式色彩，官方头衔更偏爱 advisor 这一拼写。

intro.en: Advisor is built on the Latin verb for seeing: advice began as making something visible to another person.
intro.cn: advisor 建立在拉丁语表示「看」的动词上：建议最初就是把事情让别人看见。

items.en: Videre meant to see, and its past participle visum supplied the stem for vision, visible and advise.
items.cn: videre 意为「看」，其过去分词 visum 提供了 vision、visible 与 advise 的词干。

items.en: Vulgar Latin advisare combined ad-, toward, with visum, giving the sense to cause to see or to consider.
items.cn: 通俗拉丁语 advisare 由 ad-「向」与 visum 组合，义为「使看见、使考虑」。

items.en: Old French aviser meant to perceive, to consider and to give an opinion, and it carried the word north.
items.cn: 古法语 aviser 意为「察觉、考虑、发表意见」，并把这个词向北传播。

items.en: Middle English avisen meant to consider or to counsel, and the noun advice grew beside it.
items.cn: 中古英语 avisen 意为「考虑、劝告」，名词 advice 随之产生。

items.en: Adviser is advise plus the agent suffix -er; advisor is a later variant spelling, now common in American official titles.
items.cn: adviser 由 advise 加施事后缀 -er 构成；advisor 是后起的异形拼写，如今常见于美式官方头衔。

note.en: The look-alike group stays inside the see family; the near-meaning group lists other people you pay to think for you.
note.cn: 形近组留在「看」这一词族内；近义组列出其他受聘替你思考的人。

entries.definition: The usual British spelling of the same noun.
entries.definitionCN: 同一名词的英式常用拼写。

entries.definition: To give someone an opinion about what they should do.
entries.definitionCN: 就某人该怎么做给出意见。

entries.definition: Worth doing; sensible under the circumstances.
entries.definitionCN: 值得做的；在当时情况下明智的。

entries.definition: An expert paid to give professional advice, often from outside the organization.
entries.definitionCN: 受聘提供专业意见的专家，常来自机构外部。

entries.definition: A person trained to give guidance, especially on personal or legal matters.
entries.definitionCN: 受过训练、提供指导的人，尤指个人或法律事务。

entries.definition: An experienced person who guides a less experienced one over time.
entries.definitionCN: 长期指导经验较少者的资深人士。

normalIntro.en: Remember advisor through advise: the advisor is the one who does the advising.
normalIntro.cn: 用 advise 记 advisor：advisor 就是做 advise 这件事的人。

normal.en: Advise plus -er equals the person who advises, exactly like teach plus -er gives teacher.
normal.cn: advise 加 -er 就是提建议的人，正如 teach 加 -er 得到 teacher。

normal.en: The vis inside advisor is the same vis in vision and visible: an advisor gives you vision.
normal.cn: advisor 里的 vis 与 vision、visible 中的 vis 相同：顾问给你视野。

normal.en: Split it as ad plus visor: a visor is what you look through, and an advisor is who you look through.
normal.cn: 拆成 ad 加 visor：visor 是你透过它看的东西，advisor 是你透过他看的人。

normal.en: Advisor ends in -or like doctor and professor, which is why official titles prefer it.
normal.cn: advisor 以 -or 结尾，像 doctor、professor，所以正式头衔偏爱这种拼写。

normal.en: Advice is the thing, advisor is the person; one is uncountable, the other can be counted.
normal.cn: advice 是东西，advisor 是人；前者不可数，后者可数。

abstract.en: Picture a foggy road and a person walking beside you holding a lamp: that lamp is the advice.
abstract.cn: 想象一条雾中的路，旁边有人提着一盏灯：那盏灯就是建议。

abstract.en: Imagine a map you cannot read, and a finger tracing the route for you.
abstract.cn: 想象一张你读不懂的地图，一根手指替你描出路线。

abstract.en: Think of a second pair of eyes borrowed for a decision you must make alone.
abstract.cn: 想象为一个必须独自做出的决定借来的第二双眼睛。

examples.en: Every freshman is assigned an advisor at the start of the term.
examples.cn: 每位新生在学期开始时都会被分配一位指导教师。

examples.en: The advisor warned that the investment carried serious risks.
examples.cn: 顾问警告说这项投资带有严重风险。

examples.en: She works as a legal advisor to several small charities.
examples.cn: 她担任几家小型慈善机构的法律顾问。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「额的歪泽」——额（ad）头一歪，泽（visor）出一双眼睛替你看路，这人就是顾问。

root: 拉丁语 ad-「向」加 visum（videre「看」的过去分词）构成通俗拉丁语 advisare「使看见、使考虑」，经古法语 aviser 进入英语 advise，再加施事后缀 -er／-or 构成「出主意的人」。

sensesIntro.en: All three senses keep one image: someone else sees the situation clearly and tells you what to do, whether about money, courses or state affairs.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项保留同一意象：别人把局面看清，再告诉你怎么做——无论是钱、课程还是国家大事。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a second pair of eyes that makes the situation visible
core.cn: 核心意象：让局面变得可见的第二双眼睛

branches.en: Seeing done as a paid profession.
branches.cn: 把「看清」当成受聘的职业。

branches.en: Seeing narrowed to a curriculum.
branches.cn: 把「看清」收窄到课程地图。

branches.en: Seeing attached to state power.
branches.cn: 把「看清」接到国家权力旁边。

branches.en: Both give a recommendation, not an order.
branches.cn: 两者给的都是建议，不是命令。

branches.en: Both are formal posts with a title.
branches.cn: 两者都是带正式头衔的职位。

intro.en: Advisor is a transparent Latin build: a prefix of direction, a root of sight, and a suffix that turns an action into a person.
intro.cn: advisor 是透明的拉丁语构词：一个方向前缀、一个视觉词根，再加一个把动作变成人的后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin ad- plus visum produced advisare; English kept the verb advise and built the agent noun on top of it.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ad- 加 visum 产生 advisare；英语保留动词 advise，并在其上构成施事名词。

latinEntries.example: Videre is the source of vis-.
latinEntries.exampleCN: videre 是 vis- 的来源。

latinEntries.example: Visum supplied the stem of advisare.
latinEntries.exampleCN: visum 提供了 advisare 的词干。

latinEntries.meaning: to cause to see, to consider

definition_en: a feeling of fondness or tender attachment, or in psychology, feeling as opposed to thought
core_image: 母亲把孩子画的第一张画小心收进抽屉，指尖在纸上停了一下
scene: 老照片摊在桌上，祖母一张张慢慢摩挲。 She looked at the old photographs with great affection.
sceneCN: 这里的 affection 是「喜爱之情」（第 1 个义项：对人、事物温和深厚的爱意）；句意是她满怀深情地看着那些旧照片。

pos.zh: 名词：喜爱；关爱；情感

derivatives.zh: 去掉名词后缀 -ion 还原为动词，义为「影响；感动」
加 -ate 构成，义为「充满深情的；亲昵的」
加 -ly 构成，义为「深情地」
由动词过去分词转作形容词，义为「受影响的；做作的」

senses.title: A feeling of fondness
senses.definition: a gentle feeling of liking or caring for a person, animal, or thing
senses.definitionCN: 对人、动物或事物温和的喜欢与关心
senses.example: She looked at the old photographs with great affection.
senses.exampleCN: 她满怀深情地看着那些旧照片。
senses.why: Latin affectio named a state of being moved; when what moves you is a person, the state settles into fondness.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 affectio 指「被触动」的状态；当触动你的是一个人时，这种状态就沉淀为喜爱。

senses.title: Feeling as a mental faculty
senses.definition: in psychology, the emotional side of mental life as distinct from cognition
senses.definitionCN: 心理学中与认知相对的心灵的情感方面
senses.example: The study separates affection from rational judgment.
senses.exampleCN: 这项研究把情感与理性判断分开。
senses.why: The technical sense keeps the Latin noun's neutral meaning: any state of being moved, without the warmth of the everyday word.
senses.whyCN: 这个专业义项保留了拉丁名词的中性含义：任何被触动的状态，不带日常用语的温度。

intro.en: A Latin noun for being moved, narrowed in English from any state of feeling to warm liking.
intro.cn: 一个表示「被触动」的拉丁名词，在英语里从任何情感状态收窄为温暖的喜爱。

items.en: facere meant to do or make, the base of fact, effect and the verb afficere.
items.cn: facere 意为「做、造」，是 fact、effect 与动词 afficere 的底子。

items.en: ad 'to' plus facere 'do' formed afficere, to do something to a person, to move or affect them.
items.cn: ad（向）加 facere（做）构成 afficere，意为对某人施加作用、使其动情。

items.en: affectio named the state produced by such action, a disposition or feeling of the mind.
items.cn: affectio 指这种作用产生的状态，即心境或情感。

items.en: Old French affection carried the noun into English with the sense of a settled feeling towards someone.
items.cn: 古法语 affection 把这个名词带入英语，指对某人稳定的情感。

items.en: Everyday English narrowed the word to fondness, while psychology kept the neutral sense of feeling.
items.cn: 日常英语把这个词收窄为「喜爱」，心理学则保留了中性的「情感」义。

note.en: The first group is the affect family; the second gathers words for warm attachment.
note.cn: 第一组是 affect 词族；第二组收表示「温暖依恋」的词。

entries.definition: to influence or move someone
entries.definitionCN: 影响；感动

entries.definition: influenced, or unnatural and pretended
entries.definitionCN: 受影响的；做作的

entries.definition: moving the feelings; touching
entries.definitionCN: 动人的

entries.definition: showing fondness openly
entries.definitionCN: 充满深情的

entries.definition: a gentle liking for someone or something
entries.definitionCN: 喜爱；喜欢

entries.definition: a much stronger feeling of deep attachment
entries.definitionCN: 爱；程度比 affection 更强

entries.definition: kindly feeling shown towards others
entries.definitionCN: 温情；亲切

entries.definition: a bond of affection that ties one to another
entries.definitionCN: 依恋；情感纽带

normalIntro.en: The noun is affect plus -ion: the state of being moved by someone.
normalIntro.cn: 这个名词是 affect 加 -ion：被人触动的状态。

normal.en: affection is the noun built on the verb affect, plus -ion.
normal.cn: affection 是在动词 affect 上加 -ion 构成的名词。

normal.en: The common pattern is affection for a person or place.
normal.cn: 常见搭配是 affection for 一个人或一个地方。

normal.en: Affectionate is the adjective for someone who shows affection easily.
normal.cn: affectionate 形容一个人很容易流露喜爱。

normal.en: In psychology, affection means feeling rather than thought.
normal.cn: 在心理学里，affection 指情感而非思维。

normal.en: Spell the ending -ction, like action and connection.
normal.cn: 词尾拼作 -ction，与 action、connection 一样。

abstract.en: Picture a hand smoothing a child's drawing before it goes into a drawer.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手把孩子的画抚平，再收进抽屉。

abstract.en: See the same warmth become a laboratory term for any feeling at all.
abstract.cn: 想象同样的温度变成实验室里指一切情感的术语。

abstract.en: Imagine a bond thin as thread but strong enough to hold a memory.
abstract.cn: 想象一根细如线的纽带，却足以拉住一段记忆。

examples.en: He speaks of his old school with real affection.
examples.cn: 他说起母校时带着真切的感情。

examples.en: The child showed affection by holding her hand.
examples.cn: 孩子拉着她的手来表达亲昵。

examples.en: Psychologists often contrast affection with reasoning.
examples.cn: 心理学家常把情感与推理相对照。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿费克伸」——阿费一伸手，就把那份喜爱递到人心里。

root: 拉丁语 affectio「被触动的状态」来自 afficere（ad- 加 facere「做」，意为对……施加作用）；经古法语 affection 进入英语，日常义收窄为「喜爱」，心理学仍用其中性的「情感」义。

sensesIntro.en: Two senses keep the same state of being moved: everyday warmth towards someone, and the neutral technical name for feeling.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项都保留「被触动」这一状态：日常里对人的温暖，以及专业上对情感的中性称呼。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand smoothing a child's drawing before it is put away.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手把孩子的画抚平收好。

branches.en: a grandmother touching old photographs
branches.cn: 祖母摩挲旧照片

branches.en: a child holding a hand to show liking
branches.cn: 孩子拉手表示亲昵

branches.en: fondness for a school one has left
branches.cn: 对已离开的学校的眷恋

branches.en: a study separating feeling from reasoning
branches.cn: 把情感与推理分开的研究

branches.en: one moved state, warm in life and neutral in science
branches.cn: 同一种被触动，生活里温暖，科学里中性

intro.en: A Latin verb of acting upon, its noun, and English endings.
intro.cn: 一个表示「施加作用」的拉丁动词、它的名词，以及英语词尾。

latinIntro.en: afficere and affectio are recorded Latin forms.
latinIntro.cn: afficere 与 affectio 都是有记录的拉丁形态。
